So I got this thing home to see if it would trim to my preferred length, and no it won't. I'm liking the stubble look, and about 3-4 days growth looks best on me. This trimmer only goes down to what represents 7-8 days growth for me. I have another Panasonic trimmer that works fine, but it has the same issue. I can take the comb off and cut the stubble down to about one day's length and then let it grow back a few days, but I'm getting really tired of doing that. I think these manufacturers should specify their trimming lengths so you can do a reasonable buying comparison.

B000FEF1V4-134.review_title: Shifts beard length setting without warning
B000FEF1V4-134.review_text: My T980 does almost everything perfectly: it holds a charge for weeks; its vacuum reduces the number of trimmed hairs around the sink by about 70%; it feels wonderful and it works quickly. However, my T980 does NOT stay at the level I set it at. If I don't firmly grip the length setting wheel it will jump from, say, a 5 to a 3 -- as it did this morning -- embarrassing me either by giving me a patchy trim or by forcing me to shorten my beard length. This problem doesn't seem to be a result of the way I'm, say, holding the trimmer -- I used the [[ASIN:B0001HYL0M T765]] for four years without having this problem -- but rather a flaw in the trimmer itself. From these reviews, it seems like only a few of the T980s have this problem; still, you might want to try the [[ASIN:B000FED5D0 T780]], which doesn't seem to have this problem -- I wish I had. Update 3/12/08: Make me look like a fool once, shame on me; make me look like a fool twice, shame on you. I've used this trimmer about 12 times since writing this review, and by a combination of duct tape, a pinch grip, and a good deal of vigilance I had been able to avoid too many embarrassing shifts in beard length. ...until this morning, when it shifted silently from a 5 (Late Winter Academic Beard) to 3 (Peach Fuzz) in mid-shave. Two options: shave my entire beard to a 3, which is inappropriate for my face type, or look deranged because half of my face is at 5 and half is at 3. I threw my T980 in the garbage ten minutes ago.

B000FEF1V4-9.review_text: My Norelco T900 was great, but broke recently, so I went out looking for another one, only to find it was discontinued. Didn't see any Norelco trimmers comparible to my old trimmer. Bought a T980, took it home, and found out the first trim... its junk (I'm being nice with my wording). Overall, its too big to easily hold. Worst of all, the trim height setting moves when you press it against your face... so during my first trim, it ruined my goatee. Not a good trimmer, period. Too big, too much bling. I don't need a vacuum cleaner built into my trimmer.

B000FEF1V4-330.review_text: It seems fine for a battery operated trimmer, EXCEPT! The trimmer doesn't stay at the setting you want. So, I used it for the first time this AM, put the setting on 5 or 6, but after a few strokes on the beard, it reset itself to the lowest setting. So, one spot on my beard is now down to a stubble. So, I have to go ahead and shave the rest of my beard that short. I tested it over and over, and slight pressure resets the length mechanism. Long and short, the thing doesn't work. I'm returning it.

B000FEF1V4-484.review_text: Unfortunately, Norelco really messed up what they had right to begin with. The length adjustment does not snap into place like my old Norelco trimmer and will shift while you are shaving. If you want to get a clean shave, go ahead and purchase this product, because that is exactly what you will have to do after using it. Disappointing build quality!

B000FEF1V4-396.review_text: At first, people think this is some kinda sex-toy from the future. It's not. It's a beard trimmer. And a pretty good one to boot. If you're like me, you use your beard trimmer when you don't have much time in the morning before you have to take off for work. If you trim with this thing quickly on the 'normal' trimming mode, it'll catch maybe 75% of your hair in the vaccuum. However, when you enter warp speed (turbo mode) this thing is insane. It's really loud and sounds like it might explode, but it works great. It catches roughly 90-95% of hair in the vacuum in turbo mode. It's quite easy to take apart to empty out the little hair-catch-all and clean trimmer attachments or swapping them out (comes with a fine-line trimmer). The height adjustment doesn't seem quite as pronounced as my older Norelco trimmer (meaning you can obviously tell when it clicks into place...this one not so much) but it works nonetheless. I'm happy with it and recommend it to all who read this. Just be sure to take a minute out of your abnormally busy day to read the instructions and precautions and maintenance tips to prolong the life of this thing. That's what they're there for, after all.

B000FEF1V4-514.review_text: The trimmer works perfectly in every sense. The only thing that kills it is the fact that they decided to include an AC adapter that only works with 120 volts. In other words, if you travel, you can't charge this trimmer in most other countries. I don't think it's that much more expensive to include an adapter that accepts 110-230 volts. My last Norelco trimmer that lasted 7 years could accept 110-230 volts and was always with me in my travels. Items such as trimmers, shavers, cell phones, laptops, etc. all should accept 110-230 volts, since they are mostly travel items.

B000FEF1V4-524.review_text: If you plan to travel outside the USA make sure you have a full charge and do not run out of juice while away. It is strange this day and age that products come with 110-120v transformers one vs. 110-240v; esp. personal care items like shavers and trimmers. If you run out of power when in Europe (say) plan to have to take a AC adapter or buy a new adapter while overseas. You get a reasonable use time before re-charging, but ever now and again you will have a situation where your trimmer or shaver gets turned on while packed tight in your luggage - then you will be out of luck.

B000FEF1V4-324.review_title: I hate shaving. I LOVE THIS TRIMMER.
B000FEF1V4-324.review_text: THIS THING IS AWESOME. I AM NEVER SHAVING AGAIN. I just used it for the first time and have decided that I will never use a razor again. I am a guy who never likes to shave, I maintain the "few days of stubble" look throughout the week, and dread the day when I have to go through the hassle of lathering up & shaving. But this thing is so easy to use and it just cuts you down to whatever stubble-level you want in like 2 minutes!!!! PLUS it's got this vacuum-device on it that sucks up the stray hairs into a special chamber, which you then pull out and empty when you're done trimming. so to quote Wayne's World..."It SUCKS as it CUTS!" I LOVE IT!! I AM IN LOVE WITH THIS TRIMMER! I have never written a review for Amazon before and I've been shopping here for years! That's how fired up I am about my new purchase!!!!

B000FEF1V4-33.review_text: There have been a lot of complaints about the vacuum option of this trimmer. Let's be realistic....its not a Hoover, it's a trimmer. It catches MOST of the hairs, which is a lot better than NONE of the hairs. I've used it a few times so far and haven't had the problem others complained about where the setting is changed mid-trim. Just hold the thing below the dial, and not right on the dial. It gave a nice even trim all around. I've had it for a couple of months, used it 3-4 times, and still haven't had to recharge it. Suggested improvement - A stand would have been great so I could put it in my medicine cabinet and not have it roll around my counter. Tips for using - I found you're better off with dry hair. When the hair's wet, it's harder for the vacuum to pull it in. I also found that the vacuum works much better on longer hair then on shorter hair. Maybe the shorter hairs are too light and get blown around? Last but not least, watch out for the settings. The dial goes 1-9 so I started with 4, which was way too short. I could have grown that beard from scratch in a couple of weeks. 5 also proved a little short for me. Be sure to start a lot higher than you think you need, and work your way down if needed.

B000FEF1V4-392.review_title: Norelco blew it with the vac/trimmer/guard interface. This thing is bad.
B000FEF1V4-392.review_text: I'm very disappointed with this trimmer. The thing that made me buy it is the thing that makes this unusable. I speak of the vacuum. It does a good job at keeping the hair out of the sink, but its placement sets the trimmer so far back from the guard that using this trimmer on setting 2 (which is what I always used on my old Norelco T7500 to keep it nice and tight) is the equivalent of setting 7 or so (which is fairly long) on my old trimmer so I am unable to get a nice tight, trim look. Using it on a mustache is useless especially right underneath your nose. It is simply impossible to angle the trimmer in such a way as to trim the hair. I have attempted to use this trimmer twice and both times have had to result to pulling my very old T7500 out of the drawer and using it to get a decent trim. Even setting this thing on the closest setting (#1) the trimmer still sets back waaaaay too far from the guard to be useful. If you contort you wrists and elbows you can get a fairly close trim on setting 1, but it is a giant pain to have to keep twisting and turning this trimmer around to achieve an even halfway decent trim. This thing is done. I'm shopping around for another brand. I've been a Norelco user for over 10 years, but they blew it with this one!

B000FEF1V4-37.review_text: Now that I bought and used the T980, my cool slacker goatee is attracting too many women. I'm not getting any rest. Naturally, a product that causes grief should be down-rated, but I won't here because this shaver is just doing its job. And, we all like things with "turbo" in the description, however loosely that term is applied. It makes it go faster with a cool noise, so even in a shaver that is attractive to many. Electric shavers for beards sure beat the heck out of scissors! The Norelco has a wide range of cutting depths and my beard comes out a uniform length. I did not feel any pulling or other discomfort. The charge seems to last for days and the charger itself, like the shaver, is a decent and modern design. The little detail cutter is easy to attach and does a great job of defining the beard area and also clipping any stray hairs under the nose where the big cutter head cannot reach. Some people think the closest cutting position is still not close enough for that short-stubble look and that does seem to be the case. I don't want mine that close, but I understand those who do and I take off a star for brotherly solidarity. Actually, I'm sure that if it was to cut more closely, that would take it into the realm of regular shavers, an expensive world of high-tech blades and lubricants. Actually, if you press down a little, you can get closer. The turbo thing works well. It vacuums almost every hair into the storage chamber. I didn't expect the vacuum action to work so well. I think the turbo button should be the only button, but there it is. The non-turbo setting is less noisy... The parts detach easily and the little supplied brush works well to clean it out. The little travel pouch is nice. The T980 works just as it should, for me, and the price is reasonable. I think it will last a long time and I am glad I bought it. As for the women, I did exaggerate. One did make a favorable comment which is one more than before. That is an improvement, eh?

B000FEF1V4-40.review_title: Best if used in the USA only
B000FEF1V4-40.review_text: In this day and age when almost all portable electronic products are universal power based, I regret to inform you that the Norelco Trimmers are mono voltage and cannot be operated outside the US. The unit can be charged only from (110v /120V). Neither the Philips nor the Amazon websites point this out to buyers. Since I travel outside of the US quite a bit, it is a big hassle to use this trimmer with a voltage converter. I wish Philips would seriously consider this issue and improve on the product, hence two star rating.

B000FEF1V4-506.review_title: GREAT TRIMMER--and i read all the reviews
B000FEF1V4-506.review_text: I had an old norelco that lasted 10 years, but the internal battery only lasted about 3 minutes before i finally threw it out...this trimmer is a huge step up with cutting and the vaccum. there is NO way for the guard to drop to a lower setting unless you turn the setting dial--i guess all the negative reviews where the setting dropped while in use were on a different model? works great and i am glad that i bought it...i am really picky and read all the reviews and was a bit skeptical...so im writing now to tell you that for under 40 bucks, you cant go wrong. This thing should last me a long time (it comes with a 2 year warranty) and will pay for itself becuase it allows me to keep the beard/goatee at my corporate job and fight the man!

B000FEF1V4-278.review_title: Good, but not as good as predecessor
B000FEF1V4-278.review_text: This T980 trimmer does everything nicely, but not as nicely as the discontinued and no longer available Philips Norelco T-3000. There are more beard length settings on this one, but you can't easily see them like you could on the T-3000, and more settings are not really needed. This one has a micro-trimmer which has to be installed, instead of the pop-up capability on the T-3000. This one has a turbo speed which the T-3000 didn't have and which I don't need and have never used. In short, the company has replaced an excellent product with one that is only good.

B000FEF1V4-347.review_text: I got mine around three weeks ago. The good news is that it cuts my beard well, and the vacuum is not noisy. The bad news is 1) the controls are positioned such that I find myself accidently hitting the on/off switch as I am shaving, no huge deal but annoying, 2) the vacuum action catches 95% of the hairs but 95% means you still have to clean up afterwards so it is of dubious value, and most importantly 3) it does not hold its distance setting. I find that, as I shave, the shave length setting can very easily be pushed down so that I end up with a much shorter beard than I intended. I can't imagine why after all these years Norelco has not come up with a better system for locking down the shave length so that it does not get changed by the mere act of shaving. In my opinion this last issue makes it a dud product that fails at its intended function, and I would recommend against buying it.

B000FEF1V4-335.review_text: Bought this to replace an older model Norelco trimmer without a vacuum function. Cuts well, I notice no problem with the height adjustment not staying locked in selected setting as others have mentioned. Vacuum function definately works well. I find it a little bit noisy in turbo mode. My only complaint, and it's not really a complaint, is I did like the simplicity of my older model in just removing the hair comb to use the trimmer head for the detail work. Because of the vacuum attachment you can't do that with this trimmer, you need to remove the comb, and then replace the trimmer head with a smaller trimmer attachment that sticks up past the vaccuum catch. This attachement works well, but it is a little on the small side and I'm still getting used to it. It works fine, but I wish you didn't need to go that extra step of switching out the trimmer blades. If you don't really care about the vacuum function you might want to keep in mind that trade off. Overall, I am very pleased with the purchase, and you can't beat it for under $30 shipped.

B000FEF1V4-575.review_title: This thing sucks and I love it.
B000FEF1V4-575.review_text: I was skeptical about the vacuum capabilities when I first read about it, but after trying it I must admit that I'm very impressed. It literally catches about 90% of the hair, so there's way less to clean up after. I'm a hairy beast so I usually use it a few times a week and so far it's been great. If I was attracted to beard trimmers I would date this one because it's sexy looking and cleans up after me. Great price for a great trimmer.

B000FEF1V4-179.review_text: I was apprehensive about buying an expensive trimmer, and wondered if a less expensive one would do the job of just keeping the goatee that I wanted to just the right length - just a stubble length. I did buy some cheaper models, but they turned out woefully bad, so much that I dropped the idea of keeping a goatee and just went with clean shaven for a while. But then I read all the great things that I read on this and decided to go for it. BEST PURCHASE !! I can have just the right length of trim that I want, in fact, I found that the shortest trim is a bit too short, it just gives the 5 o'clock shadow - so if thats the look you want, you wont be disappointed !! I use the # 2 length setting, and thats just right for a stubble - just enough to feel, but too short to actually grip any of the hairs. I love the vaccuum feature, and although its not perfect vaccuum, you have to shave over the sink if you dont want stray bits of hair on the floor.. few hairs do escape the vaccuum, but use the trimmer for a few weeks and then check out the chamber, you would be surprised how much has been caught in. the fine trimmer attachment is ok, not so great to do the fine lines of a goatee, I got to do it quite a few times, but then I suspect nothing will ever come close to the perfection a blade can offer. This is as good as it gets ! Go for it, you wont be disappointed.

B000FEF1V4-218.review_text: I bought this trimmer because of it's built in guard and vacuum capabilities. I've been using it about once a week for the past 4-5 months and have been extremely satisfied so far. It does not catch or pull while trimming and I've had no difficulties with the guard slipping to a lower setting as others have reported. The vacuum works great catching most of the trimmings. It does leave a few trimmings on the sink but those are few enough to simply rinse down the drain with no worries.

B000FEF1V4-339.review_title: Decent Trimmer, Poor Vacuum, Guard Slips
B000FEF1V4-339.review_text: I purchased this trimmer for my husband and he likes it for the most part. It trims evenly, is quiet and handy. It vacuums most of the hair, but he still has to stand over the sink because of the mess it makes. Otherwise, it's been a good buy, no problems yet. Follow-up: We returned the item because the guard slips. I would like to give this product a 1 star.

B000FEF1V4-459.review_title: Overall a great trimmer with 1 exception
B000FEF1V4-459.review_text: I've been using a Norelco beard trimmer for years. I bought the first T100 which used 2 AA batteries. I've seen the improvements over the years and they have definitely added to how well the products functioned. Right off the bat I'll tell you my exception. This beard trimmer was made in China. That might not matter at all to some and you are entitled to your opinion. But it matters to me and I was slightly disappointed to see that they are not being made in Austria anymore. Other than that, I am impressed with this trimmer. The turbo vacuum system works great. I have not had to clean my bathroom sink even once. The self-sharpening blades no longer need to be lubricated with oil. Ever though this unit is slightly bigger than my last one (T990)it is not more awkward in my hands. Even the Accu Control System's flexing guide comb is easier to clean than the last one. I do have to recharge the battery after 2 or 3 uses but it does have a quick charge feature that takes about 1 hour. So I can't really complain about that. I have not noticed any problems with actually trimming my beard. The 9 lockable length settings have not slipped for me as others have reported (I am currently using a number 4). I have not had any problems with trimming under my nose but I have been used to using a Norelco. Some trimmers are still made in the USA like Wahl but some of the features in this Norelco I have not found in other trimmers like the vacuum trimmer feature. If this Norelco was still made in Austria I would have given it a 5 star rating. But other than that it is a good beard trimmer and I am enjoying using it.

B000FEF1V4-157.review_title: not as good as the trimmer on my Norelco shaver
B000FEF1V4-157.review_text: I've had a Norelco 8000 series shaver with a trimmer for awhile. When I grew a beard, I bought this unit based on the reviews I read here at Amazon. It's true that because of the vacuum, there is less hair in the sink. But the quality of its trimming is far below that on my Norelco shaver. If I'd known then what I know now, I would have passed on this item. It may be good for those who don't have a Norelco shaver with the trimming feature, (and don't want to pay a hundred dollars or more for such a shaver). But for those who have such a shaver, this product is, at best, superfluous. January 29, 2008 It's not even a year later, and it has broken already. I'm not a happy camper.

B000FEF1V4-480.review_title: Flex comb is a joke, Charger is a brick that won't stay in the wall
B000FEF1V4-480.review_text: Bought this to replace my Norelco T-1000 (then found out I could have bought a replacement battery for 10 bucks)which worked just fine until the battery died. The decision to buy was mostly impluse, though I did check Amazon's ratings, but I forgot to read the lowest ratings first! I keep a close cut beard or stubble, so I don't need the adjustable settings above maybe # 3 ... I also don't care about having a vacuum cause I trim over the sink and just rinse it out. Seems like they concentrate on that feature more than the basic design. Not impressed. The "contour" spring loaded thing is a joke, I removed it. The charger unit is so bulky and heavy that it will not hang on the wall socket. I have to use an extension cord from the wall and set the "brick" charger on the counter. Did not like the feel of the unit right out of the box either, it feels rather cheap (which it is), unlike my old unit. It's fairly large and and bulky, like the charger! Don't know what the blue plastic floating shield thing is in front of the cutters, but it makes hard to judge depth when trimming without the adjustable guide on. I'll use it for the time being, then donate it to the thrift store when I find a better unit. Not worried about paying forty bucks, as I can afford to toss away cash at the this moment. Got free shipping too, unlike Ebay sellers that are charging 20 bucks to ship!

B000FEF1V4-241.review_title: Registration and Customer Service already a problem!
B000FEF1V4-241.review_text: I am so mad about trying to register for this trimmer for warranty service on the Phillips Norelco web page that I can't actually say whether or not the trimmer is any good. I went on the web page for registration and they require you to answer a full privacy invasive survey to register the product. When I refused to do the survey to register and complained through the webmaster contact I then get an answer back from Phillips wanting me to waste my time calling an 800 number for Norelco - we all know how those calls go!! At least with the 60 day money back guarantee maybe I can calm down and decide if I like the unit - sure don't like the service so far!!!

B000FEF1V4-217.review_text: Until recently, I had been using a Remington beard trimmer I had received as a Christmas gift from about 5 years ago. The Remington was good but it eventually just couldn't go any longer so I had to search for a new trimmer. I found the Phillips Norelco T980 fairly quickly and was impressed by the good reviews. And it didn't disappoint! The shipment came quick and I got to test it out (waited an hour for it to fully charge) to see how it would perform and perform it did! The shaver comes with 9 different preset trimming sizes so there is plenty of room for dynamic trimming. The flexible trim guard was something I immediately noticed and enjoyed, since my previous trimmer did not have this feature. In addition the flexibility really does allow you to get a precision trim really easily as it contours to the face great. The T980 comes with a 2 bristle (one soft, one hard) brush for cleaning out the clippers but what really is unique about this trimmer is the vacuum that is attached to it. The vacuum is made so that there is less of a clean up once your done trimming your beard, although it doesn't catch all the trimmings it did catch most of them and clean up was much faster than what I am used too. It also comes with a smaller clipper attachment for precision sculpting or just your run of the mill mustache trimming which is slid on and off with ease. The shaver also comes with a Turbo Mode but the only thing this really does that I have noticed is give the vacuum more power, it may also speed up the clippers but I am not sure about that it seems to clip nicely whether the Turbo Mode is on or off. I think because of the vacuum this trimmer seems a bit louder during operation than my last trimmer but by no means is it a chainsaw (haha). Finally, the trimmer comes with a travel bag for easy storage on trips which I thought was thoughtful. The only qualm I had was the packaging...it comes in a really sturdy clam shell package and with no helpful opening tabs so it could take you at least a few minutes to get everything out without cutting yourself on sharp plastic edges but since that has nothing to do with the performance of the trimmer I wont go on about that. So all in all, this trimmer is a fine replacement; dare I say upgrade to my last trimmer, it is said, "You get what you pay for" well, with the Norelco T980 I think you may be getting that and then some! Precision trimming, ease of use, and convenient clean up and features makes this shaver a must buy for any man especially those on the job hunt!

B000FEF1V4-301.review_title: Doesn't do what I need - returned it the next day
B000FEF1V4-301.review_text: I bought this to replace a 4 year old Norelco G390 which served me reasonably well for the past 4 years till its NiCd battery died (bought at a "warehouse" store for just under $20). There are over 600 reviews with an average of 4 stars and I thought "how can 600+ people be wrong?" so I bought it. Dumb idea. I won't go through all the pros and not even all the cons so you'll need to read other reviews, I'll just focus on why I simply can't use it and had to return it: 1. The distance from the comb interface to the blade - the part that goes up and down and stays at the same distance from the blade - is 1/8 inch longer than on the G390. This is due to the vacuum duct. As a result I was simply not able to get all the way up my mustache to trim it - it simply hit the nose. Other angles of approach or even the lowest trim setting didn't work. I was left with a funny looking longer part of the mustache and looking like a dictator from the previous century which i will not name. I ended up taking the comb attachment off the blade and, using a real comb like hairdressers used to do, trimmer the rest of the way manually. Suffice to say I did not pay $[...] so I could do that. I'll post the image comparing the G390 to this one on Amazon and you can see for yourself how it limit the reach of the blade. 2. The vacuum is useless. Sure, it capture a lot of the hair but enough of it drop out too. There is no way I would use it anywhere else but over a sink and even then I'll have to clean both the sink and the little transparent bin - so why pay extra. I've returned it to Amazon the next day. I'm going to look for the G390 or another similar model from Norelco - the G390 was about half price, didn't have vacuum or direct AC but did have multiple attachments, upright stand and lasted 4 years despite the antiquated battery technology.

B000FEF1V4-131.review_text: I purchased this product because blades are too expensive these days and I'm just not a morning person. I like the stubble look so after searching product reviews, purchasers of the 980 seemed confident in it's ability to take care of business on setting #1. It does a great job, 90% of hair gets sucked into the trap. No facial irritation. The only thing you may need is a regular razor to shape your beard's edges. With the length guard removed you can get pretty close but if you want no hair there you'll need to resort to trimming to zero length then shaping with a razor (while not perfect in that it can't do it all, the results are perfect)! Pros: Light reasonably quiet no oiling! grip it by the twist height adjuster and it works great Cons: doesn't have a foil-like shaver attachment for removing hair to zero no stand/dock (only a neg for people who have no place to hide it) not a smart charger I believe it's an old style battery so don't expect it to last as long as lithium

B000FEF1V4-51.review_text: Yep - this thing is awesome... The zero feature makes it look like you shaved that morning and the stubble has just barely started to grow in, and if you wanted to be completely hairless maybe you should have asked to have been born a woman. The battery lasts for weeks and the vacuum, though loud, is EXTREMELY effective. The decibel level of the vacuum should not bother any red blooded man who enjoys going to sporting events and screaming at the top of his lungs, or watching a dragster blast down a quarter mile in 4 seconds. This thing could chisel the beard off of Chuck Norris AND Rosie O'donnel in one charge!

B000FEF1V4-462.review_text: This beard/head trimmer works as you might hope it would. I had purchased, about 3 years ago, a version of the same trimmer and the battery eventually stopped holding a charge for very long. The old version was an AccuVac T870. I got another trimmer to replace the old one and it did not have the "Vacuum" part and my wife was not happy about the "little hairs all over" (even after I tried to clean up) -- so I returned that one and looked for a similar one to my old one. That is when I found this one on Amazon and got it. Great upgrade from the "older one" I had. Every feature I liked from the old one is still there but it has been improved in many ways as well. The old one took 12 hrs. to charge and this one takes 70 min. The adjustment "clicker" (how close to trim) is firmer, so there is less chance of it moving on you while you trim (making for a shorter than expected cut at times - a risk with the older one). What totally amazed me is after the first initial charge (following instructions) I let it drain the battery until it indicated it was time for a charge (neat new flashy light thingy does that), but it let me use the trimmer for full trim (I do my head and my beard) about 6 - 7 times before it needed to be re charged. This one also says it can be used while plugged in. The previous version never said it could be and I used it that way at times which may have compromised the battery for the old one. Now I feel fine using it plugged or unplugged since the instructions say it's OK. I like it, no more "little hairs all over" -- of course a few leak out here and there, but I usually do a good enough job to keep my wife happy with a little wipe down around the sink, etc. after trimming. I don't even use the "Turbo" switch but perhaps if I did there would be no hairs around at all. Good Product, get one. I really like mine.

B000FEF1V4-390.review_text: I have had this item for almost three months now, and I am quite happy with it. Noting some of the issues in other reviews, I would have to add: - The battery is adequate. I use it every five days or so, and it holds a charge for close to a month. - I have a close cropped beard, and keep it that way using level 3. Setting it to levels 2 or 1 will give you the "couple of days growth" look. - The vacuum picks up more than 90% of the clippings, leaving the bathroom sink nearly hair free. I suspect that buyers who are having trouble with this feature have longer beards, and longer hairs might not be caught as easily. The razor does everything I wanted it to do, and I would purchase it again.

B000FEF1V4-156.review_text: I ordered this trimmer as a Christmas gift for my husband. I was particularly interested because the reviews stated it could be used plugged in or unplugged and that the vacuum feature was effective in reducing the level of flung trimmings. He had worn out a trimmer of another brand which had done a minimally acceptable job on his beard and mustache. He loves this one. It is easy to use, not too noisy, and lives up to its billing.

B000FEF1V4-122.review_text: I've trusted Norelco for years, and this product doesn't disappoint. Trimming is easy, the vacuum feature is very convenient, keeping your bathroom counter and sink hair-free, and the multiple trim settings is also a plus. The only gripe is that it's loud, especially first thing in the morning, but it's not a big issue to me.

B000FEF1V4-429.review_text: I've had a beard for about 28 years and used manny a trimmer. This is the best trimmer I've ever had. There's very little mess and does a great job. I find no fault with it, been using it for over 1 year.

B000FEF1V4-323.review_text: It's have dual voltage charger, so you can use it (with an adapter) in every country that support 110-240v from outlet.

B000FEF1V4-498.review_text: Only tried it once so far -- for beard trimming -- but it's very promising. The "mowing" operation -- getting my beard to an even length -- went extremely well. It was easy, the results were good, and the vacuum did a surprisingly good job of capturing most of the trimmed hair. The "edging" operation was a little less successful, but I think that new personal care products like this always take a little while to get used to. I'm optimistic that I'll go from liking it to loving it with a little practice. And the battery ran the trimmer strongly throughout that first session. It's a Ni-Cad battery, so you KNOW it will disappoint you in the end, but: - The instructions are very clear about how to maximize a Ni-Cad battery's life. - You can always fall back to corded operation. (That's a smart design.)

B000FEF1V4-587.review_text: I just bought the Norelco T980 after reading many reviews from many different products. I had previously a BabyLiss product that lasted 3 years and then the battery died. BIG PROS: - Great vacuum. Takes over 95% of the hair. - Corded in addition to Rechargeable Battery. That's just great, because in 2 years time, if the battery dies, you can still use it. - Very comfortable in the face. - Nice design. COMMENT ON CONS: - In some reviews I read that the minimum length (1) is not short enough. I was a bit concerned before buying it, because I like to have a very short beard. Nevertheless, I find it PERFECT. It leaves you a beard of around 1mm length, so I DON'T THINK THAT'S A PROBLEM.

B000FEF1V4-560.review_text: I find that the smallest setting--#1--does not give a real stubble shave. After about five-days without shaving, the trimmer would not cut anything when set at #1. The only way I can get a closer shave is to take the head attachment off and shave with the blade exposed, but this can result, and has resulted, in bald spots where I've tipped the blade too close to my face. This also defeats the vacuum function.

B000FEF1V4-319.review_text: Ok I took note of the reviews and some issues folks had with this model and I still purchased it. What is worse is even though I found that I disliked the same things as others I kept it, and only after the 60 day return did I decide I didn't really like it enough to use it. So I am at fault, but I don't want others to make the same mistake. The length setting is easily shifted while in use. There is a plastic part near the blades which moves up and down when pressed against your face, why not just have it stationary? I removed the plastic piece and then when I went without it I got the 5 o'clock look when I set it on a 3 which is odd. The vacuum does work well (when in turbo mode) but I really didn't need it. I donated it to the veterans, and I hope they get some use out of it. I then went to target and for 25 dollars (10 less) I purchased the remington mb-300, which is much like the old norelco I had but better in several ways. If anyone is thinking of purchasing the t-980 please reconsider and get the remington mb-300.

B000FEF1V4-608.review_text: I misplaced the guide comb attachment on a trip, and despite the fact that every other Norelco trimmer's guide comb is easily purchased online, it is impossible to find the T980's guide comb. Nice trimmer, but I really can't use it now.

B000FEF1V4-304.review_text: The Philips literature says the lowest (#1) setting trims your beard down to stubble but this is just not so. Mine isn't close to that. Overall, the trimmer has a lot of positive points (quiet, efficient, vacuum works well, etc) but this is a big drawback for me.

B000FEF1V4-320.review_text: I must say that I disagree with most reviewers on this product. I have several problems with the design which I would like to share. First, a disclaimer. The product title says that it is a hair "trimmer" and not a "clipper". Perhaps I did not see the distinction at first, but I see that others purchase this unit as a clipper as well. So, as a trimmer (used very frequently and with very short hair trimmings) this unit may work for you. But even as a trimmer, if the hair is cut at any length (and there are 9 settings to the guide), this thing is useless. First, the "on" and "turbo" buttons are too easy to push while handling, and I'm constantly startling myself with the turbo setting (it is a little loud). Also, I find that the guide/vacuum design is poor. This may work OK if you are trimming short guide settings, but if you get a clump of hair in the guide, which happens constantly with me, it will block the tiny opening for the hair cup. The vacuum is not strong enough to pull the hair in, and it clogs the whole works. If you do not notice this, the blockage will prevent the trimmer from trimming, and you may think that a lower guide setting is needed. You can see how this sets you up for a scalp job when the low guide setting is finally low enough to make a cut. I just find the whole set up "gimmicky" and I will take the old standard guides and no vacuum any day. It does have a strong battery and if you are just lightly trimming a mustache or a beard, it may be the right choice for you. I think people like me would not be disappointed (and would not have purchased the product) if it had been called the Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Beard and Mustache Vacuum Trimmer. Long title, but descriptive enough to avoid purchasing the wrong product.

B000FEF1V4-437.review_title: A veteran trimmer says "Not at all what I was hoping for"
B000FEF1V4-437.review_text: I have had several trimmers over the years, and while I'm still using this after 9 months, it isn't what I was hoping for. My biggest issues are as follows... The beard setting that determines the length of the beard can shift unknowingly to a shorter length as the trimmer is pressed to the face. Also this unit cannot trim the area of the mustache just beneath the nostrils - I still need to use scissors. Finally, it is not easy to remove the beard length piece to perform a close trim right above the lip. I would not recommend this and I am only leaving this review as I am on Amazon looking for a new one.

B000FEF1V4-481.review_text: I've used this trimmer for about the last two years. It does the job pretty well. However, recently the removable hair catching unit got stuck and, when I pulled too hard, the plastic broke. I checked Norelco's website but the catcher didn't show up in the replacement parts list. I then called Norelco and was told that the hair catching unit is not an available replacement part. It seems absurd that the only removable part on the unit, a part that is removed regularly as a part of its function, a part that is made of fragile plastic, would not be available for replacement. This means that because I broke two cents worth of plastic, I now have to toss out a $40 beard trimmer. I'm now looking for a trimmer with no removable parts and, preferably, without the Norelco name on it.

B000FEF1V4-563.review_text: I've had the Older model of Norelco very plain, simple and still working. This one has too much bell and whistle but not as good as the older model. I would've returned it back to Amazon if shipping wasn't an issue.

B000FEF1V4-333.review_title: Amazing Trimmer... that doesn't hold the trimming level.
B000FEF1V4-333.review_text: I was incredibly excited to get this trimmer. I previously had a Norelco Trimmer that I absolutely loved and thought worked wonderful. After a few years of use the battery didn't hold much charge and I finally lost the charger after traveling! I looked at the trimmers available and the Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer sounded great. I was a little worried about purchasing it however because I read some users were having problems with the trimming guard moving position. I thought I'd give it a try and if it didn't work, I'd send it back... and ultimately I was hoping the people having troubles were just incompetent. I charged the trimmer for a day. Played around with the trimming guard by pushing on it and moving it up and down and it seemed to be extremely solid and sturdy. It seemed like it locked in position just fine. After starting to trim on a safe level 6 (my goatie had gotten long, waiting for a new trimmer) I was having success. While gliding the trimmer up the side of my goatie, WHOOPS, it slipped to Level 4. Oh well, I said, I guess I'm going to have a level 4 goatie. Well to sum it up, about halfway into it I was surprised with a slip to level 2. The vacuum is wonderful, it works perfectly. But honestly, do you really give a crap if you have to shave at a level 2 every stinking time? Why didn't I send it back? The package was impossible to open, I had to cut and rip it in shreds. It's hard to go without a trimmer but PLEASE read this review and know that you WILL have problems with it slipping trim guards, I guarantee it. The design of the trim guard dial is part of the problem. I'm not going to sit here and tell Philips how to design a trimmer though, they've done it correctly in the past. BOTTOM LINE: Great idea, new innovations work great, but as a trimmer this is a piece of junk because you can't shave at any level higher than a number 2 without risk of ending up 2 levels lower or MORE.

B000FEF1V4-394.review_text: No good for a goatee.It won't fit under ones nose for mustache trimming. It's just to big and bulky. Might be good for shearing sheep. Don't be fooled by the money back guarantee, you still have to pay for shipping and insurance.

B000FEF1V4-14.review_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Beard and Moustache Trimmer
B000FEF1V4-14.review_text: This is a nice beard trimmer. However, it appears that the trimmer I received has a defective rechargable battery.

B000FEF1V4-433.review_title: Observations from a previous Norelco owner:
B000FEF1V4-433.review_text: This unit does an entirely adequate job of beard trimming. The settings match up well with those from earlier units and, once set, there is no slippage from one setting to another. In my estimation, the "turbo" feature adds no functionality, only noise and increased battery drain. The new vacuum feature allows for the capture of only about 60-70% of the hair trimmed. A potential positive is not having to oil the blades, but only if this does not shorten product life. And as with the last trimmer I owned, the NiCad battery is not replaceable, but it should be. The battery is the size of a standard AA but it is soldered in place. Directions are given as to how to remove the battery prior to disposal, but Norelco could have gone the final step and made the battery replaceable. My old trimmer worked fine; only the battery needed replacing. But then again, I would guess that product longevity does not rise high on the list of marketing features.

B000FEF1V4-147.review_title: Good grimmer, not so good spares
B000FEF1V4-147.review_text: Excellent unless you need spare parts. Obsolete immediately

B000FEF1V4-472.review_title: The trimmer blows hairs into my eyes, and its ...
B000FEF1V4-472.review_text: The trimmer blows hairs into my eyes, and its design makes it very difficult to trim up close to my nose. I would give this product negative stars if I could.

B000FEF1V4-141.review_text: For a Philips Norelco product, it was only so-so. I subsequently bought a Wahl product and found it to be much better.

B000FEF1V4-303.review_text: I bought my first Philips Norelco trimmer in 1993 and it worked very well. Since then I have bought three more Norelco trimmers and they have all broken after a fairly short time and under quite light use. I'm looking for a better trimmer.

B000FEF1V4-195.review_text: Never really got a good shave out of this. The chamber would fill up so quickly and I could only get what I needed after several passes in turbo mode.

B000FEF1V4-417.review_text: vac isn't strong and clogs up easy other wise it is a good product. It hold charge pretty good too.

B000FEF1V4-557.review_text: I bought this trimmer in 2009 and have been using it every week since. It is easy to handle and provide a comfortable clean cut. However it is very hard to clean. The trap's hinges broke twice already. This is rechargeable trimmer with a long lasting battery (~8 beard trims) but it is not really a travel trimmer. It charges only on 110v and the on/off switch place atop tends to turn the trimmer on in its traveling bag. I ended up growing a thick holiday beard on few occasion! As for the turbo, I never figured it's use. Bottom line, it is a good value home trimmer to handle delicately.

B000FEF1V4-201.review_title: Works ok, but a wet/dry trimmer is the way to go!
B000FEF1V4-201.review_text: Had this trimmer for 2 years and it died last week after sliding into the bathroom sink under running water.... While it was working it was a good trimmer overall, though I really didn't like have to switch out the trimmer heads for the standard and then the detail sized cutters--on more than one occasion I was in a hurry and fumbling around looking for the other cutter assembly than what was on the trimmer. Another issue was that it was relatively easy to move the height adjustment by accident when taking off and replacing the plastic trimmer guard, which you need to do in order to switch cutting heads. It wasn't a really big deal, but a lot of times I wouldn't remember which number I had the hair length set on, and then I would have to guess what setting I had it one the last time I used it.....The vacuum feature was nice I guess in that it doesn't get too many little beard trimmings all over the sink, but then again it's really easy to just turn on the sink and rinse it, or, use the trimmer over a rug where you'll never see the small trimmings..... But the big lesson here is to be sure buy a wet/dry beard trimmer that won't die if it gets a little wet. I just bought the Panasonic ER224S All-in-One Cordless Hair and Beard Trimmer [[ASIN:B000F4USF8 Panasonic ER224S All-in-One Cordless Hair and Beard Trimmer (Silver)]] which was almost half the price of the Phillips Norelco unit and it's a wet/dry trimmer that you can use in the shower. It also has a built-in detail trimmer so you don't have to switch cutter heads and worry about loosing attachments. When I went to replace the T980 that died, I avoided the latest Phillips/Norelco version because I think a wet/dry is beard trimmer is really the only way to go. So far I really like the Panasonic, and I wish I had bought one of these to start with.......

B000FEF1V4-170.review_text: The blades on this are not very sharp, and the length adjustment collapses when in use. I would not recommend this trimmer.

B000FEF1V4-70.review_text: I've owned Norelco beard and mustache for years but after a ciuple of months this one would start without even touching it, The on-off button became defective. I would pay alittle more for a better quality trimer.

B000FEF1V4-491.review_text: Update: Using the Turbo mode helps substantially in vacuuming up beard hairs. However, it still doesn't get them all, so you still have to do some cleanup. I'm not changing my rating; just adding this info. It works well enough. Original ------------------- I've only had the Turbo Vacuum Trimmer for a few weeks, but my experience so far has been mostly positive. It trims well and is fairly easy to use. However, I'm also not really seeing much benefit from the vacuum part. I don't use the turbo mode and it still leaves numerous beard hairs which I have to clean up afterwards. Also, due to the added bulk of the vacuum, it's a little less precise than my old Norelco trimmer, which it replaced. If I had my choice, at this point, I would have preferred to stick with the old one (it was worn out).

B000FEF1V4-60.review_title: Might be the best out there for the $, but not terribly impressed
B000FEF1V4-60.review_text: I purchased this unit to replace a 7-year old Norelco trimmer (that had an integral main blade and an integral mini pop-up blade, but no vacuum). Good Points: Comfortable, not too noisy, even on "Turbo" setting. Strong blades clip everything in sight. Mini trimmer blade is sharp and precise. Guide pops off easily. Comfortable to hold. Vacuum does pick up lots of beard/stache clippings and it's easy to empty clippings,too. Easy to change lengths. Nice travel bag. Battery life excellent (but do NOT overcharge and obey the drain-to-zero recommendations). Bad Points: Vacuum not strong enough to suck up all clippings...you'll still need to trim over a sink or trash container, which really takes away from the advantage of having the vacuum (even on the Turbo setting). Length indicator needs a stronger click-and-hold ratchet mechanism -- too easy to accidentally change length settings. I miss the pop-up mini trimmer: Having to manually swap out blades is a pain. The trimmer can't stand up, even temporarily...it can only be stored in the bag or lying down. Summary: This trimmer might be the best compromise of cost / features / functionality out there, but was disappointed with the vacuum capabilities even on Turbo. I was very impressed by the cutting quality.

B000FEF1V4-196.review_text: Trimming - It always leaves some stubborn hairs which do not get trimmed, especially if the beard is a bit longer. Vacuum - not good enough still I have the mess to clean afterward.

B000FEF1V4-360.review_title: Excellent but this model still uses Ni-Cad battery, badly in need of an update
B000FEF1V4-360.review_text: I've been using this one for two years and I have loved it. But I must say the battery is still old-fashioned Ni-Cad and the product itself hasn't been updated in years. Come on, in this day and age you can't get away with not changing a design for three years.

B000FEF1V4-251.review_text: I had a Norelco trimmer for years, and it worked quite well. When it finally died, I bought this as a replacement. What a disappointment! The cover over the blade is either too thick, or poorly placed. Either way, the result is that no matter how close a trim I want -- that is, no matter what the number on trim closeness I use -- I get a mediocre result. It doesn't go close enough -- not nearly close enough. I wind up having to take off that cover, which makes it really hard to get an even trim. Very disappointing, especially after years of satisfaction with a trimmer from the same company.

B000FEF1V4-286.review_text: Unfortunately I have to agree with some of the more critical reviews of this product. I say unfortunately, because the vacuum actually works pretty good when the unit is new. But ask those people who rave on and on about this unit how well their trimmer is working after a few months use and i bet you will get a totally different answer. The suction power substantially decreases after a few months of use it and it drops clumps of hair every where. And this is despite cleaning the unit thoroughly after each use. There are just too many other problems with this trimmer to recommend it. Most namely, it keeps breaking. I'm on my fifth unit in 3 years. Luckily it does have a 2 year warranty and Philips/Norelco has been terrific at replacing them. But, still, this continually breaking is a problem. I think this is mostly due to the cheap plastic build. I also agree with another review in regards to the ON/OFF and Turbo buttons being in a bad location. Because these buttons are where the fingers naturally sit to hold the trimmer I'm constantly, unintentionally, turning the trimmer off. This is very annoying. And I too have had the unit change to a shorter setting during use. Also very annoying.

B000FEF1V4-517.review_text: The power and trimming of this razor is fine. My issue is with the plastic cover that holds in your beard trimmings. Mine falls off easy, spilling the trimmings over the floor. Also the trimmings jam in the narrow vacuum slot. If you do something like take off the cover and bang out the razor over a trashcan, you will lose the filter in the trash can. I have adapted by trimming with my finger holding the cover on, and banging it out while holding onto the filter.

B000FEF1V4-318.review_text: After all the other reviews I read on this I guess I expected too much. It's another piece of China junk. The on/off switch is too large so it's constantly getting turned off in use. The adjustable attachment for length fell off between cutting strokes & I gouged me beard. That sucked! I was expecting a better trimmer.

B000FEF1V4-165.review_text: Like many other reviewers, I experienced the annoying nuisance of the trimmer length setting decreasing with normal pressure applied while trimming. This is really a huge problem. I have cut my beard too short twice as a result of this design flaw. Norelco should send us out new trimmers, guys! I also agree that the vacuum is a waste, as unless it retains most of the hairs (which it doesn't), you still have to clean up the sink. Finally, having to manually change out the trimmer head to trim your mustache, ears, etc is a pain, and really not all that easy. I like the older design with a flip-out small trimmer head for the latter functions. The T980 is an example of "newer is definitely not better". Back to the drawing board, PLEASE, Norelco.

B000FEF1V4-87.review_text: I bought the Philips Norelco T908 Turbo based on other customer reviews. I wish I hadn't. The thing is a piece of junk. The swivel adjuster for setting beard length moved when I was using it and suddenly I was cutting off more than I wanted. Also, the plastic catcher broke after about a month. Avoid this like the plague!

B000FEF1V4-275.review_text: The Norelco T-980 price was not much more than the cost of replacing the battery in my 10-year old Norelco Maverick T-3000 and I was excited about the addition of a vacuum feature. Be careful what you wish for! The vacuum does its job and sink cleanup is definitely faster. But the vacuum feature tends to obscure your view of the blade edge making it much trickier to aim the thing at your beard's edge while looking in the mirror. The vacuum must be emptied by using thumb pleasure to disengage one side of a rather flimsy, curved compartment cover that swings open on a hinge that looks so weak that I'm afraid it's just a matter of time before I accidentally break either the hinge or snap the cover in half. Equally delicate-feeling are the two sliding, plastic prongs used to hold the primary blade in place. Yet it must be removed each time one wants to use the smaller, more accurate trimming blade. And of course the trimming blade uses similar prongs to hold it in place. My older T-3000 had a self-contained trimming blade that slid forward with a simple thumb push whenever needed and then retracted just as easily. The T-980 is larger around and heavier than the older unit... enough so that I really miss the sense of control and precision I was used to. In short, the T-980 feels clumsier, less maneuverable, and less accurate. It takes longer to complete the job due to the hassle of changing the regular blade and the trimming blade. And it really tries my patience having to be so careful not to beak one of those delicate, sliding, plastic prongs or the vacuum-compartment cover. I'm really tempted to pay the $30 it will cost to restore my old T-3000.

B000FEF1V4-56.review_title: Not as good as its predeccesor.
B000FEF1V4-56.review_text: My old T965's battery gave up after 4 faithful years of service. The problems with the new T980 are: the new body is a hard slick plastic which is more difficult to grip (slips out of the hand); the small/fine trimmer is now an attachment. That means you've got this small trimmer head that you have to keep in the medicine cabinet or when you travel in a safe place where you won't lose it; the depth indicator is hard to read and the numbers aren't always centered in the tiny viewing window. Philips has now replaced the old standard coiled power cords with specialized adapters. This means when you're on vacation you've got to bring the AC adapter for your face trimmer and then bring a different AC adapter for your beard trimmer. Pros: It looks real pretty. It cuts well.

B000FEF1V4-190.review_text: The Vacuum Trimmer is a good idea. It actually works. It doesnt get everything but most of it. The turbo is a bit loud but trust me its not the end of world. Any trimmer is going to make noise. Speaking from an African-American, the trimmer just doesnt give me that smooth trim i have with my current "Andis Professional 04710 T-Outliner Personal Trimmer". I cant speak for all men because all hair is different but speaking for most African Americans, it wouldnt work well. The coreless feature and Vacuum is awesome, but i need a little bit more. Smooth transaction. Shipping was fast.

B000FEF1V4-372.review_text: Works well as far as trimming your beard is concerned but the suction system isn't as thorough as advertised. I always end up with hair on things.

B000FEF1V4-43.review_text: My only other trimmer was a Norelco adjustable trimmer. So I can only compare it to that one. The T980 is much larger and trims quite well. The biggest drawback in my mind is when you want trim around your beard or mustache or ears, you can't simply pull off the plastic guard and expose the blades. You must replace the guard with a much smaller head that has exposed blades designed for this purpose.

B000FEF1V4-294.review_text: this blade when used without the trimmer ,is rough crappy metal that snags and pinches your skin and pulls your hair, to the extent of blood..

B000FEF1V4-371.review_text: I had a Norelco T780 Vacuum Trimmer before this one that I returned to Norelco under warranty because of a defective battery issue.Kept maybe a 10min charge. Noreclo sent this one as a replacement.It is a nicer model. As far as trimming goes, does a fine job.I'm not a huge fan of the AccuControl System with flexing guide comb.Wish it were just a simple non flexing comb.I used to get a more precise shave from my oldest original trimmer especially near my moustache.To the nitty gritty. If you trim very very slowly, the vacuum feature does a pretty nice job of picking up probably 80-90% of the trimmed hair.If you work in real time, it's performance is sub par.If you use the turbo feature, it is still not that effective. You will get hair on your counter and freak out the wife if you haven't wiped them all away..This trimmer is probably one of the best out there though..

B000FEF1V4-404.review_text: Just like T970 this clipper has some design flaws that make it a poor choice for trimming. The zoom dial adjusts by itself even with the slightest pressure while trimming giving an uneven cut and closer trim than was desired. It needs to have a setting lock or the dial in a different location than right where you hold it. The vaccum function is so-so, I could live without it. Noise level is unusually high, but that's least of my concerns.

B000FEF1V4-114.review_text: My first impression at taking my $44 trimmer out the box, was "Gee, this feels cheap." But I was impressed by the vacuum (which does collect a good 80% of the hair) and thought I'd try it out for the 60 day money-back time period. That time has come to an end and I've decided the nifty vac is just not enough. The huge trimmer head makes it impossible to cut evenly under the nose. Also, the "Flexing Contour Guide" requires one to push the shaver fairly hard against the face for an even shave. This wouldn't be a problem were it not for the "Lockable" length settings which it turns out is not very lockable. It's alot of fun when you realize that what you thought was length 3 has suddenly become a length 1 shave. The battery only lasts for about three shaves (maybe less considering how many times you have to go over the same patches to get everything even). And last, but not least, my original impression of this being an overpriced piece of cheap plastic does count. I'll be shaving my beard for a very long time to come, and something tells me this shaver ain't gonna make it.

B000FEF1V4-306.review_text: Functionally, this trimmer worked fine. Not even sure they make it any more. However, I have a problem when the design philosophy is based on designed obsolescence. When the rechargeable battery on this unit (and I owned two of them over the years) finally failed to recharge the product's life is over. I does have a cord but won't run off a wall outlet if the battery won't recharge. I've been left with two perfectly mechanically functional beard trimmers that will no longer run because of the design. I find such design decisions reprehensible from an environmental perspective, and shady from a business perspective. Has Norelco fixed this in their more recent models? Don't know. I won't buy the brand any more.

B000FEF1V4-552.review_text: This is a great machine, but the vacuum is far from perfect. It is still a messy procedure, don't think that the vacuum will keep your bathroom clean. It might still be worth buying this model over the one $10 cheaper, because in addition to the vacuum, this model works plugged in when the battery is drained.

B000FEF1V4-573.review_text: This was a complete waste of money. It doesn't cut the beard hair evenly and the length guide slips so that it will suddenly cut your beard down to nearly bald with no warning. The craftsmanship feels flimsy and on the shortest setting it scratches up the skin. The suction feature doesn't work well and you end up with hair everywhere to clean up. Please save your money and buy something that works!

B000FEF1V4-273.review_text: One of the worst products I've every purchased. Poor design clogs easily and requires frequent and messy cleanings to keep in operation. Even then, it takes forever to cut anything. My older Braun still does a better job (after 8 years!) than this does after one. Don't be seduced by the specs an neat-looking design. Where it counts, this fails completely.

B000FEF1V4-146.review_text: I had a Norelco trimmer that lasted several years and loved it. The main reason I chose the T980 over the T765 is that it can be operated from the plug. However, the comb is difficult to re-attach after cleaning and ultimately busted completely after less than 2 months of use. The vacuum is a nice feature but the receptacle is not secure, sometimes sending hair flying everywhere. The worst part is the vacuum feature makes it impossible to use the bare blade to trim edges; you have to use a separate attachment for this. The button to operate the "turbo" feature (totally unnecessary) is extremely cheap and came off the first time I pressed it. Norelco / Philips trimmers are definitely the way to go, but don't shell out the extra money for the shoddily designed extra features. Get the T765, I just did as a replacement for this piece of dung.

B000FEF1V4-276.review_title: still comes apart. Needless to say I am as disappointed as I could possibly be. Be warned, DO not buy this product; you will be
B000FEF1V4-276.review_text: I had the same or a similar model probably for a decade. When it died, I couldn't find the same brand or model for quite some time. This one cost me about $300 from the seller. It was a completely outrageous price, but I talked myself into ordering it. Within the first month, The door to where the beard hairs are collected broke, then to he adjustable beardguard, along with several of the parts on the inside that can come out for occasional cleaning. I have had to put big thick rubber bands all over it to keep it together, but it still comes apart. It is unusable. Needless to say, I am as disappointed as I could possibly be. Be warned, DO not buy this product; you will be sorry!

B000FEF1V4-368.review_title: It's getting a bit rusted out but I liked it a lot
B000FEF1V4-368.review_text: I bought this in 2010 for under $40. It's getting a bit rusted out but I liked it a lot. So, I want to,replace it. It's now almost $300! I'm not paying that. Looks like I'll have to,join the Taliban, ZZ Top,more become a rabbi. None of those choices are attractive to me. Aargh!

B000FEF1V4-176.review_title: The vacuum misses a lot, collects maybe 75% and ...
B000FEF1V4-176.review_text: The vacuum misses a lot, collects maybe 75% and misses the rest. Plastic pieces are brittle and prone to cracking. Recently, started turning on by itself in the middle of the night. Leave it uncharged now so it doesn't wake me and just use it with the cord. I'd try something else.

B000FEF1V4-108.review_text: the latch to the vacuum receptacle broke almost immediately. otherwise, it has performed well. charge lasts a long time.

B000FEF1V4-202.review_text: The vacuum feature would be great if it got all the hairs, but it only gets some of them, so kind of pointless. You're still going to have them on you and the sink either way. The blade leaves my beard hairs so sharp that if I stroke my beard they penetrate my skin like splinters and I have to dig them out of my fingers with tweezers agh! Is this the same as all other trimmers or are these blades especially bad? The plastic part of the cutter broke and was $27 with shipping to replace. Now the plastic of the comb part broke and I'm not going to bother replacing it. These problems have occurred over a 5 year span though, so that's pretty typical for plastic American crap?

B000FEF1V4-13.review_text: These are okay but the plastics are prone to failure in small details that are required of a complicated device. Frustrating. Contour feature of beard comb no longer contours and door to hold hair opens at will. Expect 1-2 year life span max.

B000FEF1V4-461.review_text: I've gone through several other beard trimmers, and was very excited about the features this one provides: adjustability, turbo vacuum, EASY-adjust, ability to use corded OR cordless. However, in practice, I've been very frustrated by this one. Adjustability was fine. The easy-adjust ring was nice. It functioned great plugged in or not. The problems I encountered were: 1 The swing-out door to empty the clippings broke. It's cheap, and has barely any material supporting it. It's not like you can just tape it closed, because you need to be able to open it. 2)The spring-loaded trimmings hatch stuck open, and lost its spring. So, even holding the clippings-door closed, trying to "make-do" and not have to discard this so soon, is very frustrating because the trimmings don't get captured - they stay at the top and spillover the trimmer. 3)The turbo has no extra sucking effect. It's useless. 4)The turbo is too easily turned on by accident. 5)The turbo is LOUD.

B000FEF1V4-283.review_title: Really struggles (doesn't properly do the mustache) due to the prongs.
B000FEF1V4-283.review_text: Decent settings, decent battery life, turbo button is required - and not an option but the reason I gave it two stars is because it simply cannot do the mustache area because the prongs hit my nose. I've found I have to remove the prongs and then very cautiously trim my mustache. For the beard it works as it should.

B000FEF1V4-555.review_text: I purchased this in March of 2010, about 21 months ago. I was never particularly impressed by the vacuum function. I'm sure it sucked in some of the hair, but whats the point if you still have to clean your sink? Recently it broke. Since I only used it every 3-4 weeks, that means it probably broke after about 30 uses. The springs that flexed the comb popped out. I would not recommend anyone purchase this item.

B000FEF1V4-22.review_text: It's not a bad trimmer, but it's not what I was hoping for when I bought it. I suppose my biggest complaint is how messy it is. I was really looking forward to the vacuum feature but doesn't work particularly well for me. Sure, it collects some hair, but plenty more ends up on the sink and the floor. I was hoping to make trimming a no-cleanup operation. Alas. Beyond that, seems to work as advertised. I haven't had any problems with it yet, but I don't think there's much advantage to it vs my old, clumsy trimmer.

B000FEF1V4-162.review_text: i've tried quite a few, and this one is pretty decent. i don't get the "turbo" because why would you ever want less power? so i just put it on turbo all the time. that being said, some older trimmers (that have more metal) have more power than this one. the adjustable head works well, then you can take it off for close shave. it could be closer... not the quality of a barber's tool with a really clean, sharp cut. the vacuum feature is pretty gimmicky. yes, it does capture quite a bit of hair when you're trimming a longer beard (making clean up a bit easier), but this does not mean that hair does not fall. it does and you still need to clean your sink afterward. that being said, this is still my daily beard trimmer and i don't see a need to change yet, but i would if i found a better one.

B000FEF1V4-67.review_text: After reading many reviews of this product I was sold and went ahead and ordered it. My mistake. The unit is apparently not designed for heavy, thick or long beard hair, as it does not trim that well, the vacuum just clogs up and then blades tend to pull rather than cut smoothly. The blade guard (?) just lets hair jam up against the blades, which again makes for a less comfortable trim. My plan is to now get a much simpler version of this type trimmer and go back to trimming as I have always done it.

B000FEF1V4-483.review_title: Has a faulty latch on the hair compartment door. ...
B000FEF1V4-483.review_text: Has a faulty latch on the hair compartment door. A year or so ago they replaced it at no charge but it just broke again.

B000FEF1V4-98.review_text: I enjoyed this trimmer at first, though I should say that it never cut as closely to my skin as I wanted it too. But after a year, the motor started jumping and though it works, it doesn't work as well.

B000FEF1V4-167.review_text: This trimmer is a joke. I purchased it to replace an older Norelco for my husband. The vacuum does catch some of the hair but there is still hair all over him and the bathroom after he has used it. He doesn't like the feel of it and he finds it difficult to get an even trim. Worse, the plastic guard broke off after six months The only good thing I have to say about this trimmer is it holds a charge for seemingly forever. Purchase a different trimmer, this one is not as good as you hope it will be.

B000FEF1V4-279.review_text: I really wanted to love this trimmer. Especially given the hefty price tag. It trims as you would expect and the vacuum works well and is a must-have feature in my opinion. Another must have feature is either Ni-Mh battery or the more expensive Lithium ion battery. This has Neither it is the bad/cheapo/old Ni-Cad (Nickel Cadmium) with all the memory effects and shortened life span that implies. For a device like this where you can't swap the battery yourself and you can't leave the job half done you will have to partially charge and then finish your trim. Then you will recharge it fully, boom instant battery memory and shortened life. Or maybe you re-charge it after every use? That may be even worse... I've been through this before, you are doomed to a useful life measured in months before the battery (and therefore the whole trimmer) craps out. I researched on line and couldn't discover what type of battery it was so I went in person to my local WM and looked at the packaging, still no hint. So I bought it thinking they couldn't possibly sell it at such a high price point with such an unsuitable battery. I got it home and found in the instructions that the battery is Ni-Cad and soldered into place and must be disposed of properly. I'll be returning it and looking for a different vacuum trimmer with a battery that will be useful for longer than a few months.

B000FEF1V4-532.review_text: I gave this product one star because the trimmer works very well, but I have had many trimmers that worked very well. What I expected when purchasing this product, and it does cost a lot more than most, is the vacuum that it advertises to work, and it clearly does NOT! Oh it does suck some of the hair into the chamber, but it left just as big a mess of the trimmed hair all over my bathroom counter, as all the other trimmers, that don't have one. That to me is unacceptable, and I think Norelco should not be allowed to advertise as such!!! Don't waste your money!

B000FEF1V4-338.review_text: The Norelco trimmer that I bought around five years ago just died on me so it was time to buy a new one. I really liked the old Norelco so I thought I would get the same brand. This trimmer had all of the features that I wanted and I figured that since the price was so high it must ba a great trimmer. Boy was I wrong. I have a fairly thin curly beard that this trimmer just could not handle. It would not cut some places at all. Using the hilarious "turbo" button just makes it louder and does nothing for performance. After leaving my beard a patchy mess I decided to just shave the whole thing. Even with the guide off it could barely shave my beard. This trimmer is virtually worthless.

B000FEF1V4-512.review_text: This trimmer is marketed toward facial hair and sideburns, and that's all it's good for. Anything finer than coarse facial hair jams up the vacuum system, so forget about buzz cuts or body grooming. When the vacuum part is backed up, it blocks hair from entering the blades, forcing you to clean it several times per trimming session. The vacuum is weak at best, and left me cleaning up almost as much hair from my counter as my previous, non-vacuum trimmer. Although I've enjoyed Norelco products in the past, this one has been a disappointment and will be on its way back to Amazon tomorrow.

B000FEF1V4-238.review_text: I suppose I would still recommend this, but it's not all that it's cracked up to be. It cuts well, but it doesn't catch as much as it billed to. In addition, I cannot ever use it in the non-turbo mode, otherwise, it won't catch anything. Still recommended though, it keeps it a lot cleaner than without, just a little disappointing...

B000FEF1V4-148.review_text: I scoured the net looking for the perfect beard trimmer to trim my beard that I brough back from Iraq. I didn't want to look like a terrorist, so I needed a trimmer to keep my beard looking civilized. I read the reviews here and was prepared for a somewhat weak vacuum- even on turbo. No big deal- I wanted results, and the vacuum was just a perk anyway. It caught maybe half the hair on turbo, so whoopie. Well, I should have paid more attention to the negative reviews! I was careful not to hold the trimmer by the click wheel to avoid accidentally going down a setting... I did that once and clicked from a 5 to a 4. I liked the 4 better anyway, so stuck with that. I happily trimmed to a 4 once a week (sometimes twice to clean it up) for the last couple months and it worked well, until just a couple of days ago when the setting slipped all the way down to 1 when I was in the middle of shaving! I went from a nice beard to the 5 o-clock shadow look! I AM FURIOUS! There needs to be some sort of setting lock that prevents it from just slipping and ruining your beard! How hard would that be? Just build the dial with a notch you can slide a bar into in order to lock it! Until they build this with a locking device, avoid it, or you could lose your hard-earned beard- just like I did!

B000FEF1V4-184.review_text: It trimmed without inflicting pain. Thats the best I can say about this machine. The setting indicator is so small I need my reading glasses to insure I've got it right. Swiching to the sideburn/edge trimmer involves removing the adjustable guide, the trimmer head, and replacing with the edge trimming head. Part alignment must be perfect of they don't fit. Replacing the guide comb requires precision as well. A pop-up trimmer would have solved those problems. The vacuum is gimmick that works more or less, but the recepticle can pop open without warning and dump lots of little trimmings everywhere. The carrying case does not seal... just a velcro flap... so when packed, bristles can get spread around your suitcase. I dropped it yesterday, and broke one of the trim heads. I was unable to find replacement parts online, and I must say I was relieved to be forced to replace this unit with a better designed model.

B000FEF1V4-522.review_text: The adjustable blade guard works well, but it leaves an uneven cut. I'm not sure how it works on beards and mustaches, but wouldn't recommend it for "touch-ups".

B000FEF1V4-255.review_title: Completely useless as a trimmer, would not buy
B000FEF1V4-255.review_text: Not sure how this thing got so many good reviews. The device is completely useless at trimming my beard, and only works on the lowest setting (which is a really close trim). Literally on any setting past the shortest setting, it won't actually trim any hair. Not sure who designed the springy gaurd but its clear just from looking at it that none of the hair actually gets close enough to the blades to get cut. I have an old razor that plugs in and has 3 or 4 different adapters, and that works a lot better. When it does cut, on the really short setting, the vacuum does actually work, but theres a plastic thing that gets in the way and makes it tough to shave with any accuracy. Anyway, hope to prevent people from having the same frustrations I have after spending $40 for something that could barely shave your head much less something a bit more technical, like your face!

B000FEF1V4-488.review_title: Its a toy. Not a real thing that can cut hair
B000FEF1V4-488.review_text: This product looks too flimsy and it looks more like a play toy. I am surprised they sell this seriously as real product that can cut hair. Hair gets stuck the minute you tried to cut the hair. Hair guard came loose almost immediately. I don't see how this product can work on full head of hair. At best it trim a beard. But I don't grow beard. So, this one is going back.

B000FEF1V4-564.review_title: good trimmer vaccume doesn't work as designed
B000FEF1V4-564.review_text: The trimmer works very well however the vaccume does not collect much. The vaccume does help pull your beard from your face which results in an even trim but if you are looking for a trimmer that requires no clean up afterwards this is not it.
