B00MZT4UEG-318.review_text: Wasn't what I expected it's very small wish it was bigger.

B00MZT4UEG-430.review_title: It's much smaller than I expected and a little softer ...
B00MZT4UEG-430.review_text: It's much smaller than I expected and a little softer than I had anticipated.

B00MZT4UEG-410.review_text: Bristol’s are soft. The larger brushes are more stiff giving the expected experience.

B00MZT4UEG-120.review_title: ... stars is no fault of their brush it was good quality but a little smaller than I thought
B00MZT4UEG-120.review_text: Three stars is no fault of their brush it was good quality but a little smaller than I thought. thank you

B00MZT4UEG-498.review_title: 3A or Above Hair- Not for you.
B00MZT4UEG-498.review_text: Not really what I was expecting. The brush is much smaller than I expected it to be- which is really not a problem. My problem is the texture of the bristles. This brush is EXTREMELY soft. It brushes down the top layers of my hair but does not give me the sleek look that I like. Would recommend to someone with fine and easy to manage hair, definitely not someone with 3A or above hair.

B00MZT4UEG-235.review_text: Smaller than I thought and didn't brush that well.

B000FEIOHW-426.review_text: This item worked wonderfully for about 1 month, then water must have gotten into it or the battery connection went bad. I would have to change the battery every week, later, realizing it was not the batteries but the connection. A cheap replacement for the real thing.

B000FEIOHW-434.review_text: This brush is awesome. I've had mine for well over a year now and it is still going strong. The other reviewers that speak of the water getting into the battery compartment; they are correct, it is a poorly designed watertight compartment and the rubber o-ring does tend to stop sealing correctly after you change the batteries out one or more times. However, I have come up with a very simple solution: when you first get the toothbrush, remove the end cap and lubricate the o-ring with plumbers grease. Granted, I'm sure alot of you do not have plumbers grease handy and if that is the case, petroleum jelly will work just as well. Make sure you apply liberally to the o-ring all the way around and once you place the cap back on, you can wipe any excess from the outside. Voila, now you have a watertight seal that actually seals.

B000FEIOHW-55.review_title: Fix the leak issue, and the toothbrush is superb
B000FEIOHW-55.review_text: Since I originally wrote this review, I bought 5 of them, over time. All are still working. I've used Sonicare since before they were bought out by Philips. One thing I hated in over 15 years of owning them is the battery dying out, it lasts about 5 years, and I've gone through 3 versions already. While a new brush will hold a charge for over a week, after 3 years, it will give about 3 days sometimes not, so if you travel with the brush you'll also have to lug the charger, otherwise you'll have a useless brush with no power sometime in your trip. The brushes still use NiCD, so you get a memory effect and to revive it you have to recharge best when the brush is dead; to do so you have to endure the increasingly weak brush stroking and it dying sometime while you brush. You can't just leave it on, all Sonicare's have a 2 minute timer, Quad Pacer or not. This AA powered Sonicare I've had for 1.5 years, and it works as good as the rechargeable versions except it doesn't have Quad Pacer, not a problem. As a brush, it has the vigor and thus, the benefits of what made Sonicare famous. I was concerned about Amazon reviews of water leaking into the battery compartment. I've tested the brush since then, and found what the weakness is; not cleaning the battery compartment O ring seal after each battery replacement. Like many items used for water, you should clean the battery compartment O ring and its sealing surfaces thoroughly before resealing it. The head usually has toothpaste on it that is abrasive and gritty and will break the O ring seal if not washed clean out. All a user need do is during a battery change, use an old manual toothbrush to brush clean the open end cap until its clean of all debris. Wash the O ring with soap and water. Let both air dry to avoid getting lint on the cap or ring. Use a clean finger to wipe clean the interior battery compartment to insure its clean or clear of residual toothpaste, as this is the other half of the sealing surface that contacts the O ring. When ready to seal, take a tiny dab of vasoline or silicone O ring lubricant between your thumb and forefinger, and pass the O ring through these fingers so it has a light coat of lubricant. This prevents the o ring from twisting as you insert the cap, and breaking the seal. Place the o ring on the cap, and push on the Sonicare. That's it! I use NiMH batteries, and a new set lasts over 2 months, brushing once a day. I can even use my old used NiMH cells on this brush, and I get about 1 month. The O ring should last over 5 years but if you know O rings, it AS568A size is -023, change them every 2-3 years. These rings typically cost 1c each, but the problem is finding them, usually they are sold in industrial supply houses. The toothbrush has held up, so it won't die because of leaking or bad battery. For $25, this unit is an ideal Sonicare. Now if only the brush heads were cheaper.

B000FEIOHW-466.review_text: Dont buy this. Other Sonicare products are good but this battery operated is not worth your money. Reasons: This will stop operating when the water enters to the battery compartment. No matter how you do, the water enters the battery compartment and causing short circuit. Second, the plastic bottom that closes the battery compartment will break and no longer can be secured. Just dont buy this. I dont understand how they could come up with this design. If the bottom of the battery closure is of spin closure type, then it would be much better.

B000FEIOHW-335.review_title: A short length of electrical tape and you're good to go!!
B000FEIOHW-335.review_text: A short piece of electrical tape resolves the water infiltration issue where the battery base connects with the brush holder. My experience with the rechargeable units was that they lasted for 2-6 months and then died. Phillips was pretty good with warranty service but the no charge replacement handles again lasted around 2 months. For the AA battery model I recommend fresh alkaline batteries rather than reusable/rechargeable AA's. The battery contacts in the brush handle sometimes dent the battery electrodes and can interrupt the connection. Fresh AA's quickly resolve that issue. I probably get 2 months from a set of AA batteries. The brushing action is exceptional and this Sonicare provides strong performance and great value. Seal the battery compartment from water with electrical tape whenever you load fresh batteries.

B000FEIOHW-365.review_text: Although I am definitely on the 'Sonicare' bandwagon in so far as this product's ability to clean my teeth--it does a great job--this model brush is made quite poorly. The battery compartment (the e3000 uses 'AA' batteries) on mine, regardless of it having an o-ring on the door, seems to be continually wet inside, with the negative (-) terminal on one of the AA-cells rusting after only two weeks use. Philips acknowledges this is a problem but offers no solution. Also, there are many small crevices in/around the nameplate on the side, and a large gap under the nut for the brush-head that accumulates 'gook' on a daily basis. Philips advises that this is probably 'mold' and the brush should be 'disassembled and air-dried' after every use. It takes longer to do this than to brush my teeth-- Again, while this is probably one of the best ways to clean your teeth at this point in time, and an economical way to try one of the products that normally start out at $64e (and up), there is no reason why the e3000 shouldn't be made as well as the better units, or hold up to water/daily use as well as some of the $9 Crest electrics we commonly see.

B000FEIOHW-239.review_title: Great for travel and dorm life
B000FEIOHW-239.review_text: We bought this toothbrush for travel because we didn't want to carry the charging base from our other Sonicare toothbrush. It has been great. Uses the same brush heads, just operates on AA batteries. The batteries last long enough for a 2-week vacation - I don't know how much longer they'll go. My son took one to college, too, so he didn't have to worry about recharging one more electrical device.

B000FEIOHW-224.review_text: My old Sonicare died after and few years and I had tried using several different brush types, manual and powered, attempting to find a cheap replacement. After a less than stellar annual check-up, I decided to just buy another Sonicare. I saw this model and could not believe how little it cost. My old one was over a hundred dollars. It worked great too. I saw no difference other than the lack of the quadpacer timer thing. Unfortunately, it died in less than two weeks. And no, it was not the batteries, the thing is just dead. I suggest you buy a rechargable 4100 for forty or fifty dollars. I have been using one for a few months now with no issues. It has the great cleaning action of a Sonicare at a reasonable price. Same as with the cheap battery powered model, the brush turns off after two minutes but does not have the quadpacer or any other fancy features.

B000FEIOHW-260.review_text: I am really happy with it. This works just like the Sonicare units with the charging stations, except that you change the batteries. It uses the e-series heads. It does not have the reduced speed on initial use which may be a problem for first time users of sonicares. The bottom pulls off to put the batteries in. The edges that you need to hold onto to remove the battery cover are a small making it a bit difficult to remove the cover. The only downside is how fast it goes through batteries. The information on the product does tell you that it will go through the regular batteries quickly. I was getting only 3 days or so which I thought was little too fast. Lithium batteries last several weeks when the sonicare is used by one person. I give it 4 stars because of the battery compartment cover and the battery use. If you are already using a sonicare type toothbrush this is one to consider

B000FEIOHW-41.review_text: I am enjoying this toothbrush. After a good brushing job, my teeth feel almost like i left the dentists. The 'sonic waves' really do dislodge plaque and leave a very clean mouth. Great for me because i travel frequently and do not feel like carrying a toothbrush charger. One odd thing, though, is that my first set of batteries only lasted a week. I just put in a second pair of batteries and am waiting to see how long they last. I brush twice a day, so ordinary amount of usage. I tried a pair of fully - charged NiMH batteries today (I think all NiMH rechargeables are 1.2 V) and the tooth brush would not start. Seems that it needs 1.5V batteries. It worked fine with ordinary alkaline batteries.

B000FEIOHW-366.review_text: I've owned this toothbrush for nearly a year now and have no problems. I do, however, recognize the limitations of the design. If you expect to be able to rinse off the handle or submerge this toothbrush, you will be one of the many disappointed reviewers. Now, I owned two previous sonicare toothbrushes and I was never really happy with the life of the internal batteries. This is the reason I decided to go with this unit and I have not regretted my decision. My 12 year old daughter has also had this toothbrush for almost a year now and NO problems. While I do believe there could be inconsistencies in quality control, I think one can work around these shortfalls. Here's how I believe I've managed to keep my sonicare running. 1. I don't put the handle under water, only the part that goes in my mouth 2. I ALWAYS make sure to place a little vasoline on the O-Ring when I replace the batteries 3. I fling the water off the brush after I rinse the end off. 4. I don't leave the brush standing up. This prevents any residual water from running down the handle. I always leave the brush laying out flat/horizontal. Now, I realize one shouldn't have to do all this stuff to keep the brush working properly but, for me, it's a small inconvenience considering I have the ability to change the batteries. Bottom line. I really like my toothbrush but the design is not bullet proof.

B000FEIOHW-207.review_text: I have been a user of Sonicare for about 10 years--since I had a roommate who had to have gum surgery for gingivitis, and her oral surgeon recommended switching. They do a fantastic job. The price is excellent on this model, but I was concerned from previous reviews that it might not do as good a job as the regular Sonicares and that it might get destroyed from water leaking into the battery compartment. While I was trying to decide, I used one of those disposable-type battery-operated brushes you can buy for a few bucks. My teeth felt disgusting compared to when I was using a Sonicare. Since I could tell such a huge difference, but money is really tight, I decided to get this model, and just try not to get the battery area wet, and live with the lower power, and hope that it doesn't die too early. And I'm really glad I did, because I couldn't be happier with this brush. The design must have been updated because there are no holes near the battery housing as previous reviewers described (there are no holes anywhere). I'm pretty uncoordinated but without really trying I haven't gotten water anywhere near the battery area. I do blot the brush head dry on a towel between brushings, and that might be key since no water drips down the handle after I put it away. It feels just as powerful to me as my previous Sonicares, and my teeth feel just as clean. I like not having a charger taking up one of only two outlets in my bathroom and collecting dust on the counter. And I love that for travel I'll just be able to throw this in my bag without lugging a charger along. And for long travel you could just pop in two more AA batteries when needed--available almost anywhere. The batteries that came with the brush were strong, but they did die after two weeks. I would definitely recommend rechargables. Although this brush is marketed for teens or kids, the brush head size is perfect for me; I still have my wisdom teeth and with other brushes it's been very difficult to really get to them. For the price, even if this brush doesn't last a really long time, I think it will still be a very good deal. But if you buy it and it doesn't last, remember that there is a 2-year "limited" warranty. Update Nov 1 2010: Still going strong on the second set of batteries. No problems whatsoever. GREAT deal. Update May 22 2011: Still no problems, and I have only had to change the batteries 3 times since I first started using rechargables last October. When this dies I will definitely buy the same model again. It's so much cheaper than other Sonicares, and I think using regular batteries instead of a charger is a big benefit over the other models, too. Update Jan 10 2012: BUY THIS! Still working perfectly, still easy on batteries, still much more convenient for travel than other Sonicares...and considering how much other Sonicares cost, this value is pretty unbelievable. Update Nov 23 2012: OK, so I let my guard down and have now used this toothbrush in the shower many times. NO PROBLEMS! Since many reviews still complain of leakage or short lifespan, I can only assume there is a quality control issue and I lucked out. Still, for less than $30 with a 2-year warranty, I totally would have put up with one or two lemons. Update: April 2013--SERIOUSLY, BUY THIS!

B000FEIOHW-336.review_text: This product is good while it lasts; it'll clean your teeth better than almost anything out there (unless you have tartar, then you'll need something with a bit more power) and stimulate your gums. However, having autopsied this model, I am convinced that it was engineered to fail under typical conditions after a time, perhaps to motivate the purchase of a more expensive model, which will itself become useless when the irreplaceable batteries go out. The first one I bought lasted a year, and even that long only after I learned that you have to plug the two holes in the back of the battery compartment to prevent the corrosion from taking place. By the end, batteries were lasting one week tops, at 2x use per day. I also learned that you have to hit it against hard objects when it won't turn on and sometimes then it'll go. You also need to scrape off any rust from the battery contacts occasionally. Knowing these quirks, I bought another one and immediately plugged up the holes in the back and put tape around the battery cap. However, it has now lasted only a month. There's no rust or corrosion to speak of, however, it just doesn't turn on anymore. Today I autopsied the first sonicare to see why it had failed (the new one is still on warranty). In taking it apart, it's clear that most of your money goes into buying a tank-like shell around the $1 worth of electronics. This would be a good thing, if there were not two gaping holes in the battery cap that let water in anyway and the shoddy rubber seal. After taking it apart, it's clear why the corrosion so quickly leads the failure. They protect everything on the circuit-board from corrosion by putting glue over it, except the battery contacts, and the contacts and wires that lead to the solenoid coil (that makes the brush vibrate). The contacts that lead to the solenoid and the battery contacts are also strategically located next to each other on the circuit board, so they can corrode together quickly using any moisture from the adjacent battery-terminal holes, while the non-essentials like the timer are located on the other side of the board and completely sealed off from the ambient air by glue. This also explains why hitting it sometimes allows it to start; you're shaking some of the corrosion loose. The switch is also of questionable design, being nothing more than a paper-thin piece of plastic with some kind ring on it that's slightly more conductive than the plastic. If the replacement that I get out of the warranty fails, I think I'll try a cybersonic or an oral-b; hopefully their teams of engineers weren't paid to make something less reliable than a politician. Why can't they make a sonic toothbrush with no batteries, that plugs into the wall, and lasts a lifetime? Or just quit making these to fail so readily?

B000FEIOHW-143.review_title: Great brush for short money. Perfect for travel.
B000FEIOHW-143.review_text: This sonicare operates like all the others, it just doesn't include the expensive rechargable battery and charger like the more expensive models do. Because it operates on AA batteries, the unit is susceptible to some water entry if one is careless. It shouldn't be necessary to tell people not to get electric appliances wet, but apparantly it is. The handle should never be exposed to water. It is not submersible. The only portion of the entire device that should get wet is the brush-head. Remove the brush-head after every use, wash it thoroughly, and dry it. Wipe the handle dry. That is it. Take care of it like an electric hand mixer. You remove and clean the mixing pieces, you don't dunk the motor assembly in the sink. You wipe it clean. No water means no corrosion. The directions clearly state that the motor assembly/handle is not water-proof. Others have found that a #33 o-ring seals the battery compartment very well. It is an excellent, inexpensive preventative solution to water entering the battery compartment. Phillips does not include the following warning and disclaimer, but perhaps they should: Item is not idiot proof.

B000FEIOHW-419.review_text: This is my fourth electric toothbrush (my first Sonicare), and it is the best I have ever owned. For several years I had heard that Sonicare makes a good product; but the price for a toothbrush whose rechargeable batteries couldn't be replaced, made me reluctant to try one. Well, the introduction of this product made my purchase a "no-brainer," and I couldn't be happier with it. My son owns a more expensive version, and the brushing action/speed are identical. The first week of use was a "ticklish" situation. The ultra-high speed vibration does startle one at first, but after a few days the tickle disappears. I know this is subjective, but the Sonicare makes my mouth does feel cleaner than it has with other toothbrushes. Some reviewers have complained about the battery compartment not sealing well, but this has not been a problem for me. I don't drool when I brush, so water rarely gets to the battery hatch opposite the business end. I am also amazed that two AA alkaline batteries last almost three months. Now that I am on my third set of batteries, I know this much for sure. I don't want the expensive version of the Sonicare because it offers no real advantages (just bells and whistles), and I will continue to use this toothbrush until I have to replace it with another Sonicare just like it.

B000FEIOHW-355.review_title: Cost doesn't end with just buying the toothbrush...
B000FEIOHW-355.review_text: You'll be putting new batteries in this toothbrush every 2 weeks. However, if you don't mind buying stock in batteries, this is a great product.

B000FEIOHW-309.review_title: I love that there are no recharging station with cords to ...
B000FEIOHW-309.review_text: I love that there are no recharging station with cords to bother with. I use rechargeable batteries which need recharging about once every month with everyday use. I use a compact recharge unit for recharging AA batteries. And it works just as good as the higher priced models. It's a real shame that this model has been discontinued and replaced with another portable AA battery operated model that is very much inferior to this model. I first purchased this model for a very reasonable price of $29.99. Since it has be discontinued, it seems to still be in demand because the price has tripled.... that is, if you can find one at all. This purchase was for a backup to the one that I've used for over a year and have had absolutely no problems... ever. I saw many complaints about water leaking into it causing battery corrosion. Common sense says to keep it out of water except for the brush tip and dry it after every use. Fantastic product!!!!

B000FEIOHW-422.review_title: Use a little common sense, folks!
B000FEIOHW-422.review_text: I'm sorry but I just don't see how all these people are getting so much water into the battery compartment. Are you submerging the whole thing just to rinse the bristles? Are you spitting up all over it? Are you holding it vertically while you brush/rinse? Are your kids dropping it in the toilet? I've had mine two months and don't have a bit of trouble holding it so the bottom end never gets wet...or the brush end of the head either, for that matter. Just rinse off only the brush itself holding the brush end DOWN. Use a little common sense and take care of your things, for heaven's sake people. It doesn't take a genius. edit - I've now been using mine once or twice a day for over two years and have had NO problems with water leakage, corrosion, burnouts or breakdowns. Rechargeable AA batteries last up to 6 months and I change the brush/head once a year although I'm not sure it needs it even then, the new bristles feel just the same as the old ones, despite Sonicare's recommended 3-4 month lifespan. At $12-15 a pop I'm sure Sonicare would like you to replace them far more often than really necessary. No special o-rings have been needed. I still can't understand how so many people are reporting water leaks & corrosion unless they just need special supervision to operate any mechanical device.

B000FEIOHW-200.review_text: Been using this brush now for a few months now - love using it! Cleans like crazy, but isn't too harsh on my gums or anything. One thing I've discovered though is that it needs *good* batteries. When I put new, but cheap, batteries in, it acted like they were already dead. I actually changed the brush head assembly out too early because I thought something was wrong with it, when in fact putting *good* batteries in solved it. Note that when there isn't enough juice, it doesn't slow down, it just randomly turns off. Love the brush overall though :) EDIT After reading some of the other reviews, thought I'd mention a few things. I minimize/prevent water damage to this by: 1. Use the minimum amount of water that I need 2. Shake the bristles after use and wipe off the whole thing with a paper towel 3. Store it immediately, don't leave it laying on a wet counter or anything. I don't do anything particularly special for storage - just put it in a drinking glass on the counter with our other toothbrushes. Obviously I make sure there isn't a pool of water in the glass. Just what I do - seems to work for me.

B000FEIOHW-220.review_title: Just don't leave it in standing water, Einstein
B000FEIOHW-220.review_text: First point: the sonicaire toothbrushes, as a group, are worlds better than any other electric toothbrush out there. Second point: the actual brushing mechanism of all the sonicaires is the same, so think hard before you waste the money on the more high-priced brushes in the line. The various bells & whistles cannot possibly be worth the astounding mark-up. Third point: when the built-in battery of a more expensive model goes bad (and for me it went bad inside of two years), you're screwed. There's no option but to throw it away and buy a new one (though I've seen videos of people cracking open the case & replacing the battery, but really who's actually going to do that?). The xtreme is the best bargain out there, not only relative to other electric toothbrushes or other sonicaires, but on an absolute basis, considering how much money you'll save on dental bills over the years if you use it faithfully. And to those who grouse about the fact that this model is susceptible to water infiltration, I say DUH. It's an electronic device, and its battery compartment is near the base! Keep it away from water, just as you would any other gizmo.

B000FEIOHW-201.review_title: The best value in the Sonicare line
B000FEIOHW-201.review_text: With Amazon now selling this directly for < $20 this is the absolute best value in the entire Sonicare line. You get the same drive, the same brush head compatibility, 2 min timer and the ability to use your own rechargeable batteries. 5 years ago I purchased a Sonicare Elite 7300; the internal NiCad battery eventually died and the unit is not designed to swap out the battery. I tried, but ended up damaging the rubber molding and had a lot of difficulty finding a comparable battery that didn't require paying a high shipping cost. I eventually purchased the E3000 on a whim at a retail store for nearly twice what it sells for on Amazon nowadays and started using the newer low self discharge NiMH batteries. I get about a month of usage before I have to charge the batteries. And when the batteries finally start losing their capacity -- they haven't yet in 2 years -- I don't have to worry about performing major surgery on my toothbrush. I'm not sure I understand the water seepage/contacts/failure issues. I own 2 E3000s now, one for travel and one for home, and have used them both for 2+ years now. Neither have failed. I take care not to rinse the base of the unit under running water and I don't leave it sitting in a pool of water or anything. I definitely see the potential for failure as nothing but a plastic cap and a rubber gasket protect the AA batteries from potential moisture, but I think standard, common sense can prevail here. Let me stress -- I do not baby this thing. I use it daily in a bathroom that gets very humid during showers and summer weather (no exhaust fan and no central air conditioning). I clean it every usage under running water and I don't dry it off afterwards. I also have done the same types of things with 2 different E3000 units and have used them for over 2 years now and they have worked perfectly from day one. Highly recommended. I would actually feel comfortable recommending this over a higher-end Sonicare that was discounted to be within a similar price range as this unit. Being able to use your own rechargeable batteries is simply way too powerful of a feature since that seems to be the limiting factor in keeping this brushes for the long haul.

B000FEIOHW-21.review_title: Great toothbrush - replaceable NIMH betteries (you supply) is way better than non-replaceable NiCad
B000FEIOHW-21.review_text: I had mine for over 3 years. Works like a charm. It has been in luggage lots of times too. I don't recall ever dropping it in a sink full of water or with the faucet running or dropping it into a toilet or a full bathtub or running shower, so I cannot credibly deny the 1-star review complaints. I bought a bunch as gifts for my friend and his family and two of four (the ones the kids used) died in the first few months. The 5-stars is based on my personal experience. Just don't expose the battery end (bottom half) to more than a short modest spraying of water and it should last a long time for you. You can buy 3 of these for the price of the traditional model and works just as good. Get your heads in 6-packs at Costco - much cheaper 6 for the Amazon/Wal-Mart price of 4. Yes the heads are expensive but if you don't have braces or whatnot you probably can push a 6-month replacement cycle.

B000FEIOHW-477.review_text: Had I read these reviews before buying this, I probably wouldn't have purchased it. But I had been looking at the much more expensive Sonicare toothbrushes after my dentist recommended Sonicare after I asked. I didn't ask if there was a certain MODEL that he recommended, so I assumed I'd have to pay from $40-$150 for a Sonicare. When I saw this one for $30 at Target, I figured I didn't have much to lose. I've had no problems with any of the other problems mentioned and have been happy with how it makes my teeth feel super clean and has even cleaned this spot that even my dental hygienist couldn't get. It turns off automatically after 2 minutes, so I know that I'm brushing my teeth longer. One thing that takes getting used to is NOT removing it while it's going...you'll splatter toothpaste all over yourself! :D Another plus is not having your tummy jiggle like it does with a manual toothbrush!! The only negative is that it goes thru 2 AA batteries about once a month, but the directions said that it lasts about 60 brushes per battery change and that's about right. I've started using rechargable batteries and have had no problems.

B000FEIOHW-252.review_title: I have saved a lot of money and pain with this brush.
B000FEIOHW-252.review_text: I have had this for a number of years. It works great. The batteries last a long time and when they are going down it vibrates more than sonicares so I know it's time to change the batteries. I use the very small brushes and brush my Yorkies teeth every night before bed. They look great, no bad breath as long as I don't give her pork, and no need for big cost vet dental bills. This is the second Yorkie I have used this brush on. Neither one has objected to getting their teeth brushed. It is so much easier and efficient than hand brushing. I love the Sonicares for myself because it is easy to use and does a better job than I can with severe arthritis in my hands. We each have our own Sonicare but you can change the heads easily.

B000FEIOHW-248.review_text: I've had mine for over 2 years and love it. But you do need to lubricate the o-ring seal when changing batteries. I use Vaseline. This does 2 things: 1) helps the seal, 2) and this is most important, it helps to fully close the cap. If you try to close it with a dry seal, it won't full close. I suspect this is why so many people end up with water inside. I had a heigher end Sonicare rechargable brush before, but the battery died within 1 year. Replaceable batteries are the way to go.

B000FEIOHW-218.review_title: Had mine for over 2 years now. Fix for water infiltration !
B000FEIOHW-218.review_text: Bought 3 Sonicare brushes, 2 rechargeable and 1 e3000. All are doing well. I noticed the potential for water in the battery compartment. I had some silicone grease, used mostly for automotive applications. Suggest Danco Perfect Match: Silicone Grease, Amazon 88693, $0.19. Smeared a bit on and around the battery cap and o-ring. Now it is totally water tight, and changing batteries is much faster than the rest of family waiting on a recharge. Use quality Alkaline batteries, to avoid the batteries leaking.

B000FEIOHW-446.review_title: waste of money, water got in the battery compartment and corroded
B000FEIOHW-446.review_text: my first rechargeable sonicare stopped charging in 1.5 year, so I thought I will switch to AA battery operated sonicare. I thought I can use rechargeable AA battery, which would make the toothbrush last longer and it will be more green.well.. this toothbrush lasted only two annoying months. I constantly had to change battery due to corrosion. Parafilming didn't help either. going back to rechargeable expensive options. sometimes, I think the companies do this intentionally so that people switch to more expensive option. companies anyway are making money selling brush heads, why soil your reputation making bad product. Trust me, I 'll switch to another brand as soon as someone make something I like better. no brand loyalty here.

B000FEIOHW-437.review_text: Sonicare was quick to replace the origonal at no charge, however the problem is that they all broke after about one month. The last one only ran for only 2 seconds per cycle right out of the box. THere seems to be a problem with the timing circuit with this model where they shut off as soon as you turn them on. I will be purchasing a waterpik!

B000FEIOHW-387.review_text: I really enjoyed my previous Philips Sonicare rechargeable toothbrush, but after the wand stopped maintaining charge, I decided to replace it w/ this toothbrush. It was a big mistake! My rechargeable toothbrush lasted me several years. This battery-only toothbrush STOPPED WORKING no matter how many different NEW alkaline batteries I put in it. The Philips batteries lasted me almost a month, and they must be potent, "miracle batteries". When I switched to Rayovac batteries they lasted 1/2 as long. Last week, the toothbrush stopped no matter how many batteries in the pack I put in. I put those batteries into other devices to see if I somehow bought a package of dead batteries. NO. I now have the world's heaviest, impractical manual toothbrush. I wanted to try being untethered to a recharger, but the rechargeable Sonicares do go at least a week 2x/day before needing a charge. And to repeat, my old rechargeable one lasted me YEARS!!! DO NOT BUY THIS, DO NOT BUY THIS, DO NOT BUY THIS! There are cheaper comparable battery powered toothbrushes. I wasted $30 in this experiment! I will be buying another rechargeable Sonicare. Because Sonicare DOES really truly clean teeth better than any other toothbrush.

B000FEIOHW-367.review_title: Best of all worlds... just keep it dry!
B000FEIOHW-367.review_text: I have used the Sonicare Extreme for over 4 years, pretty much every day, twice a day. I've never had any problems with it at all. I use it with a few sets of Sanyo Eneloop AA's (the best!). I knew that it was prone to issues if you got it wet, so I was careful to never get it wet, and it's been rock solid. Before this, I had a regular Sonicare for about 2 years. It stopped holding a charge. That's the best part of the Sonicare Extreme. You use replaceable batteries and never have that problem. Hope this review gives you the confidence to try out the Extreme.

B000FEIOHW-226.review_title: Don't buy. I agree with other buyers.
B000FEIOHW-226.review_text: I agree with the other buyer. It's a GREAT toothbrush I loved it until water got into the unit. I purchased March 2011 and it's already broken. But when it worked I loved it.

B000FEIOHW-37.review_text: At first I thought this was going to be the solution to the problem of the original rechargeable Sonicare toothbrush with batteries that can't be replaced (my original Sonicare stopped holding a charge). However, after only four months (just long enough to waste money replacing the brush head!), the button began to only work erratically, and now it does not work at all (can't power the toothbrush on). The reviews that state that the battery compartment does not keep water out are completely true. The battery compartment is always moist, and the batteries will begin to rust. I was pleased that my Eneloop batteries worked well to power the toothbrush, so I could be using rechargeable batteries, however it doesn't matter if the toothbrush itself doesn't last past 6 months. The batteries that came with the toothbrush lasted around a month. The Eneloops needed charged only once in the next three months. Looks like the Sonicare brand just fails on too many levels, regardless of whether you are using the ultra-expensive rechargeable unit, or this unit with two AA batteries. [Update] Flashlights have had "screw on" caps for nearly one hundred hears. The Sonicare toothbrush is the same form factor. I have no idea why someone at Philips thought a "clip on" cap (vs. a screw on) would be better, ESPECIALLY for something you use with water. I am still COMPLETELY BAFFLED by why they would use this design. The battery compartment will ALWAYS be moist. Being able to use rechargeable batteries is clearly superior to being stuck with the Philips Soincare charging station. However, the fact that your batteries get wet means you will eventually ruin your batteries. That said, I am about to purchase another one. Being able to use your own batteries makes it a when, both for the fact that you can replace the batteries and also so that the (much more expensive) toothbrush isn't useless when the internal batteries fail after a year or so. Unfortunately there is no better alternative at this pricep oint.

B000FEIOHW-149.review_text: I have had a Sonicare for many years, and it was the rechargeable type. It lasted a total of 8 years, but I hear the newer ones only last about 3 years, so I chose THIS battery operated brush, and have had it for 3 months now. I read ALL the reviews herein, and was wondering why so many reviewers complained about the base not being water resistant. I have been brushing MY teeth for over 60 years now, and do NOT brush them underwater. I have no clue why someone would want to brush either underwater, OR in the shower. When this brush is used as a toothbrush, then there is no reason why it should get water in the handle. The battery compartment is located at the opposite end of the brushes, and if used normally, rinsed off, then dried with your towel, there is no way water can get into the compartment. I LOVE my brush..it stops automatically AFTER 2 minutes of brushing, and IF you use it for two minutes each time, your teeth will really be clean. My dentist tells me that my gums and teeth appear more healthy than many others they have seen, and I owe it all to my sonicare brush. BTW, I only brush ONCE per day in the morning AFTER breakfast, so if YOU use it more often than that, your mouth and gums will be healthier than MINE!!

B000FEIOHW-354.review_text: I started using this product after my rechargeable Sonicare finally died (after four/five years). I have had this toothbrush for over a year and it works just as good as the rechargeable version. This unit is much more mobile because of the battery power, can be taken easily on travel trips, is cheaper than rechargeable version, and brush heads are easily found (best price at big warehouse stores). As for other review comments, I have not had any problems with water getting in the battery compartment.

B000FEIOHW-359.review_text: The vibrating is unpleasant at first, but you get used to it. And you grow to appreciate the intense feeling because you know that it is precisely that motion that makes your teeth so damn clean. This is an excellent toothbrush. It's the cheapest of the adult brushes in the sonicare line and sonicare is way better than any other electric toothbrush. And any electric toothbrush is way better than a manual toothbrush. Electric toothbrushes are not about being lazy, they're about being time-and-energy efficient when cleaning your teeth. Example: 2 minutes with a sonicare brush makes your mouth around 75% cleaner than 2 minutes with a manual brush. Maybe 25% cleaner than 2 minutes with a different electric toothbrush that isn't sonicare. And you honestly don't need to spend $100 or $200 on one of the more expensive brushes in the Sonicare line either, since this does the same work for less money. It uses 2 AA batteries, and I use rechargeable ones, which makes it more convenient than charging the brush every night. I just swap my one pair of rechargeable AA's for my other pair when I need to, and so it is easier to travel with the brush. The sonicare technology was recommended by my dentist, and I found it here on Amazon for cheaper than what the dentist was selling it for, with the buy-from-dentist rebate INCLUDED. You could always win an eBay auction and possibly get one for cheaper than this, but I was too impatient to wait, and most auctions I saw ended around $30 anyway. Did I mention that I love my Sonicare Xtreme? Allow me to make an above point clear: If you want to spend $100-$200 on a toothbrush, then just buy 3 to 6 Sonicare Xtremes, and then give them to your family and friends. The Sonicare Xtreme uses the same brush heads as ALL THE OTHER SONICARE E-SERIES BRUSHES. These brushes are the top of the line, and the Xtreme has the exact same essential functions as the rest of the Sonicare family does, except for $100-$150 less. I recommend you don't waste your money on a more expensive brush just because it is more expensive. Do some more research and see that Sonicare brushes are the best for consumer oral hygiene. Then do more research and see that the Sonicare Xtreme has all the necessary features that the other Sonicare brushes have. Then buy it, and keep your teeth for longer. You and all the people who have to look at your teeth or smell your breath in your life will be happy you did.

B000FEIOHW-171.review_text: My first Sonicare toothbrush lasted 9 years, this one broke after 16 days, looked at the label....MADE IN CHINA!!!! It is a piece of chinese junk!

B000FEIOHW-215.review_text: I have owned two other Sonicare Power Toothbrushes over the past many years and have loved them both except for one thing. The rechargeable batteries are not replaceable. When they eventually failed, I have had to throw away the otherwise perfectly good toothbrushes. I hate waste, and this obvious scheme to shorten the life of their products to force me to buy a new toothbrush infuriated me. Now I discovered the Xtreme e3000 model which comes with replaceable alkaline AA batteries. It is intended for pre-teens and teens. I am 69, but it works great for me. Like all Sonicare Power Toothbrushes, it does a great job of removing the plaque from under the gum line and preventing gum disease. I use NiMetalHydride rechargeables instead of alkaline AA batteries. A charge lasts many times longer than the charge on the non-replaceable batteries in my previous two Sonicare brushes. I recommend it to anyone of any age.

B000FEIOHW-69.review_title: Half the cost, but more convenient than a regular Sonicare
B000FEIOHW-69.review_text: Pros: half the cost of a Sonicare w/charger, less bulky Cons: None so far First of all, I should state that I have owned this product for over a year, and I am still giving it five stars. Here's why: I had a Sonicare Advance for about three years and it worked well during that time, but at the end of those three years I had to keep it in the charger at all times or it would die in the middle of brushing. I was sick of lugging around the bulky charger any time I traveled, so when I saw the AA-battery model at Target for $40 I scooped it up. Now instead of having to rely on an internal battery and a charger, I just keep four rechargeable AAs that I swap out when one pair dies. This isn't something I have to do very often--a pair of AAs lasts about a month (that's with two two-minute brushings a day). I have also not had any water damage, so the brush still works as great as my old Sonicare ever did. I do try not to get water on the brush and dry the entire unit whenever I finish using it. In addition, I take it apart once every two or three months and swab the O-ring with alcohol to keep it clean. This seems to be all of the maintenance needed to keep it in top condition. So, if you want a good Sonicare brush that takes up less space and is easier to travel with, I highly recommend this model. I recommend cleaning it once in a while and trying to keep water out of the insides. I acknowledge this might not help if you get a bad unit (as many reviewers seem to have gotten), but mine has been great and I figure it can't hurt! UPDATE: I have now owned it for a year-and-a-half and it still goes a month on two AA rechargeables. Even though I stopped doing the maintenance described above it's still working like new.

B000FEIOHW-298.review_text: I received this as a gift for Christmas. It worked great for the first few weeks, and my teeth were noticeably cleaner. However, it then would start shutting off before the 2 min interval was up. The intervals got shorter and shorter. Then, after another week, it died all together. Don't waste your money on this cheap Sonicare, just buy the more expensive ones that are better made.

B000FEIOHW-465.review_text: I bought this toothbrush three months ago and I have had so many problems with it stopping and starting. The batteries exploding and making this really digusting and probably quite toxic mess(battery acid and all). Save your money on this one. It was a nice idea, but no where near worth the 30.00 bucks.

B000FEIOHW-185.review_text: I used to have a Sonicare a long time ago. You know, the VERY expensive plug-in one. Yes, it worked like a dream (just like they say). My DDS could tell the difference. But having another thing to plug-in in our tiny bathroom was a hassle and after about a year the charger was mucked up beyond control. Most embarrassing! Years went by and new dental problems arose. After going through the joys of a root plaining, I was looking for a new Sonicare. I saw this one and loved that it was battery operated and had a smaller head. I didn't need all the bells and whistles on the other models. Just the auto-timer. The first one that came died in 2 days. WAHHH! Amazon kicked butt and sent us a replacement right away. We've had the new one for a month now and it's still going strong. I think the first one was just defective. It does go through batteries pretty quick, so I highly suggest you get re-chargeable batteries. My DDS noticed a difference within the month. It's totally worth it, and a great price! It ends up being cheaper than the disposable electric brushes we were using. A good family brush for all ages. Easy to use, even for kids.

B000FEIOHW-219.review_text: I love this item because , I am an adult, but I have small mouth, Also it is battery operated for use, so I do not have to carry the the charger, one less thing to take with me on the road!

B000FEIOHW-237.review_text: I've had the toothbrush for over 2 months now and it works great. The battery life may appear short at first but it will improve after your second set. A little bit of water did get through to the battery housing, but did not cause an issue. I dry it every time the batteries are replaced. Final note, I believe it is as effective in cleaning as my non-battery Sonicare.

B000FEIOHW-198.review_text: This toothbrush brushes well for the price segment that it is in. It is very powerful, and actually takes a little bit of time to get used to. It doesn't really compare with the $100 toothbrushes as far as quality or comfort. The brush head is a bit small, and it goes through batteries fast. I also had it replaced once on warranty because it broke after only a week of use. The replacement appears to be OK though!

B000FEIOHW-156.review_title: Awesome! Lasted 6 years. Wish Philips still made this exact model!!!!
B000FEIOHW-156.review_text: This has been an amazing electric toothbrush. I bought it in june 2011 - its now june 2017 (6 years later) - and it worked fantastic for 6 years. Finally died a couple days ago. And I think actually it would have lasted even longer except that the contact for the batteries inside it is now rusty. I'd say from moisture over the years. I wish Philips was making still this same one. :) Because it was awesome - small brush head, vibrated well but not too hard and not too soft. I'm hunting on ebay etc for another new one or one close to it.

B000FEIOHW-30.review_title: Love these and wish they weren't discontinued
B000FEIOHW-30.review_text: Love these and wish they weren't discontinued

B000FEIOHW-132.review_text: I love this toothbrush. So far very reliable. I like the fact that it works with batteries.

B000FEIOHW-151.review_text: I am an aggressive brusher, so this really helped prevent any further damage to my teeth and gums.

B000FEIOHW-460.review_text: Just like other reviewers said: Battery housing is not sealed and water can get into it. The battery operation stopped working after 1 week. After two months there is visible rust around the toothbrush. Dont be cheap, buy a more expensive toothbrush.

B000FEIOHW-45.review_title: Good cleaning performance but bad battery cover design
B000FEIOHW-45.review_text: It does a good cleaning however the battery cover design is bad. It's snap-in type, not screw-in type, therefore water gets in so easy. After 8 months of usage, there is sign of water damage. Note that I did clean the device every 2-3 weeks. The battery cover also got corrosion that it can not be fully snapped in.

B000FEIOHW-363.review_title: If I could choose again, I would pay more to buy a better one
B000FEIOHW-363.review_text: The toothbrush is OK, but it's so annoying that the head is not sealed. So every time you use it, water will get in

B000FEIOHW-49.review_text: I've had a Sonicare toothbrush for about 15 years now and I love it. On her dentist's recommendation, my fiance wanted to give one a try. We got her the battery operated model since she was unsure she'd like it. She LOVES it though. The one downside to it - and it's a big one - is that the battery life leaves a lot to be desired. She's been using it about six months and we've replaced the batteries about six times. Had I known the battery life was so abysmal, we would have gotten her a rechargeable model.

B000FEIOHW-348.review_title: Love it but second one didn't last a month
B000FEIOHW-348.review_text: I love this toothbrush. I bought this battery one when the regular one didn't hold a charge after only a year. This one works just as good and the batteries last a long time. (I change them after two months) for those of you that are getting water in the unit there are rubber covers that go over the toothbrush head to keep water out of the threaded area. Not sure where i got them but you could try a google search. My problem was that it started to go off during use and only run intermittently. It's was my second one and it died within a month. I was going to buy another one any way when I found out that Sonicair will replace it. [...] My theory and my experience as a electrical service technician is that they have bad solder or electrical connections and since this device vibrates its very possible to shake or brake these connections. It's really too bad it's a very good device but they need to up their quality control on this model and the more expensive ones.

B000FEIOHW-244.review_text: 1. I don't understand these reviews that complain about getting water into the battery compartment and corroding the batteries. I've never had this problem. It would seem that one would have to be really careless for this to happen. Don't submerge it or pour water over it, and you should be fine. 2. Don't worry about battery life. Get some Eneloop rechargeables, and swap them out anywhere from a couple weeks to a couple months and you'll be fine. 3. This does such a good job, my dentist assumes I'm flossing like I'm supposed to be. I'm not. I do use a waterpic, but only a couple times a week these days. My dentist gave me an A+ on my last visit (part of this is because of the fluoride rinse that's been helping strengthen my teeth, but that's another review). So now to the reason I only gave it three stars. I had one of these that we bought years ago. I don't remember how long, but it's been probably 5 years. I'm not exactly sure, but it's been awhile. It's always worked great and still does. We finally got tired of sharing, and when we saw they were only $20 on Amazon we got another one. This second one has had to be replaced under warranty twice in about a year and a half. It just stopped working, both times. No corrosion in the battery compartment or anything. The unit looks pristine, it just stopped working. The first one lasted about 8 months. The second one only about 6 months. So while this is a great product (functionally) and I would still likely buy it again if my current one died out of warranty (can't beat $20) I'm getting concerned about the quality. Here's hoping third time's a charm.

B000FEIOHW-249.review_title: Need to maintain as well as your teeth.
B000FEIOHW-249.review_text: This thing is not 100 percent water tight. The seal for the battery compartment is not that great.I have put Petroleum jelly on the seal and it works a little bit better. Had it for 4 months and I had to tap the bottom of it like loading a magazine into a pistol to get it to start. Come to find out that crud builds up underneath the brush shaft, hanging it up. So I cleaned it and it works better. Ive been stripping it down completely after each use to make sure moisture doesnt build up anywhere.

B000FEIOHW-116.review_text: Unfortunately, this model does not stand up to the two previous rechargeable Sonicares I've had in the past. This one stopped working after the first week. I thought maybe they sent cheap batteries with it, so I replaced with new ones. It worked for another week then stopped again. Sending it back.

B000FEIOHW-325.review_text: As others have said, water gets into this unit very easily. I am having problems with it after only 3 months. Spend more money and get something that will last. The only saving grace for me is that I got it for free.

B000FEIOHW-470.review_text: I didn't read enough into the product to realized that it was not a re-chargeable toothbrush. Was disappointed, however for the price it couldn't have been. Anyways, for what it does, it's a pretty good toothbrush.

B000FEIOHW-169.review_text: Terrible.... I have had to replace mine twice and the third just died as well. The bottom does not seal and takes in water which corroded the batteries and rotted the entire case. otherwise it works excellent, my teeth have never been cleaner. I'm going to save myself the horror this time and spend the extra 20$ for the rechargable one.

B000FEIOHW-397.review_text: Like many of the other reviewers on here, my toothbrush was great for the first month or so. After that, water leaked into the battery compartment and caused the batteries to rust and leak. The toothbrush no longer works (4 months later) at all even after several good cleanings and replacement pieces.

B000FEIOHW-106.review_text: This would be a good tooth brush had they designed it better. Water gets inside and stops it from vibrating. Some times I have to take the top off and separate it from the bottom for a few hours for it to dry out, to get it to work. Also, gunk builds up inside of it and looks pure disgusting after a few months. I've had this about 7 months now and I'm tossing it in the trash.

B000FEIOHW-329.review_title: water WILL get into the unit - a waste of money
B000FEIOHW-329.review_text: My dentist recommended this toothbrush. I didn't want to pay the exorbitant price for the plug in so I purchased this unit. We use rechargeable batteries in my house so replacing the batteries would be no big deal. After a week of use, it stopped working. Thinking maybe I had defective batteries I replaced them. The toothbrush worked on and off for another 2 weeks then completely stopped working. Phillips did agree to send me a new one but unfortunately, that stopped working in just a few days. Water getting into the battery compartment is the problem, no matter how careful you are. If you don't mind spending 100+ dollars, buy the plug in variety as I really did like how it cleaned my teeth. Otherwise, skip it completely.

B000FEIOHW-204.review_text: Unfortunately I assumed that any problems this toothbrush had several years ago had been corrected. I was wrong. This lasted a week, despite my consistent efforts to dry the unit after every brush. Do not buy this. Spend the extra money on an electical charger unit.

B000FEIOHW-357.review_title: i loved it, but now it's dead
B000FEIOHW-357.review_text: Please believe the reviews that say this thing dies pretty soon after purchase. I bought this last August, and I absolutely loved it! I thought it worked really well, was so cute and a great bargain. Simply said, a great purchase. Now- the following March- the thing is dead. It has been working on and off for a couple of weeks now but, if I hit the side, it would start working again. Today it finally croaked. Now I have to look for a new toothbrush.

B000FEIOHW-322.review_title: Does anyone have the same problem?
B000FEIOHW-322.review_text: I really had a lot of fun for the first month I owned it. Two AA batteries lasted almost one month. Compared with other rechargeable models, this one was fairly cheap. But after 5 months, now, it's so annoying that I have to change batteries every 3 days! How come a toothbrush eats up power so crazy?! I'm thinking of buying a rechargeable toothbrush.

B000FEIOHW-467.review_text: These keep breaking. They don't last long. Less than a year.

B000FEIOHW-2.review_text: Works OK. You can go thru a lot of AA's though. We tried using rechargeables, but moisture gets inside the battery compartment, rusting and causing them to swell. My husband still uses it for business trips, however.

B000FEIOHW-443.review_text: Worked great for not even a year. These things never seem to last, cordless or not. THey leak, something happens inside. You clean them, and they buzz at low frequency at best and become worthless. I don't know what is inside these things, but it doesnt last.

B000FEIOHW-113.review_text: I bought this toothbrush to replace one which I used for FIVE YEARS. The reason it was replace was due to the o-ring in the cap wearing out, and failing to seal. Fine for five years worth of use. The new one I bought lasted approximately 2 weeks before the batteries died, and I popped it open. The batteries had leaked acid all over the compartment. Not sure if water had gotten in or the batteries were bad, but it is ruined. Before you judge me for misuse, see how I had the previous one for FIVE YEARS with no problems. I don't shower with this thing. I don't even submerse it. Total junk, and if I wasn't deployed with the military, I'd send it back.

B000FEIOHW-331.review_title: It is totally useless now. The rechargeable model will not have this ...
B000FEIOHW-331.review_text: Don't buy this toothbrush. After changing battery a couple of times, the bottom cap couldn't be closed anymore. It is totally useless now. The rechargeable model will not have this kind of trouble for you though it is a little expensive.

B000FEIOHW-485.review_text: This was the first Sonicare brush I ever bought. I really liked this until it died after about 4 months. So I went to order another one but the price on this particular model had almost doubled since I originally purchased it so I went with a different Sonicare brush. It wasn't nearly as good as this one and it lasted about 5 or 6 weeks before it died also. So this is a really good brush while it lasts which won't be for very long, so don't bother with buying replacement heads which are kind of pricey.

B000FEIOHW-282.review_title: Overall great but some build quality issues.
B000FEIOHW-282.review_text: This product seems to be discontinued now... but the build quality is real hit or miss. One worked great while another had corrosion issues with the batteries.

B000FEIOHW-261.review_title: one month and it quit working How can I get the manufacturer to replace it?
B000FEIOHW-261.review_text: caution, you may get a bad product. My second one quit after one month while my first one is still working after 2 years. The connection points seem to have rusted by water leaking in through a bad neck connection. can't return it as it is after the 30 day period.

B000FEIOHW-368.review_text: I love the toothbrush. I hate the packaging. It's in a plastic blister pack which is very difficult to open (and I'm not a senior--just a normal adult with normal strength). Once you work your heavy-duty scissors into the packaging you are left with very sharp plastic edges. It took me around 10 minutes to get the package open. Not only was it difficult (and moderately dangerous due to the sharp edges) to open but it uses way too much plastic, which will languish in a landfill for years to come. Philips, change your packaging and this would have gotten a five-star rating from me.

B000FEIOHW-183.review_text: I already own this product that I purchased from a dentist 7 years ago... it still works great. I purchased this one to use while traveling and it sounds like a lawn mower compared to my other unit. It's very loud with a strong vibration. It works - but isn't as smooth as the original. The original Sonicare I purchased for over $100 and this one cost $20... so I guess you get what you pay for!?!?

B000FEIOHW-162.review_text: It use battery, cannot be re-charged. It is kind of desppointing. I would love one which i can take for travelling.

B000FEIOHW-76.review_text: The Sonicare does an excellent job, but lasted less that 3 years. Otherwise I would have rated it 5 stars.

B000FEIOHW-129.review_text: The brush worked great for the first two months. I was surprised at how long the batteries lasted. The rechargeable ones went at least a month before needing charging. When I took out the batteries for charging this time, there was water in the battery compartment and rusting. I recharged batteries, dried out unit and put in batteries and the brush wont work no more. I have used the rehargeable versions for years without problems but this purchase was a mistake. Update Dec 1, 2013: spoke with customer service and they are sending a replacement unit. Very easy process. I will update to three starts for excellent customer service. Will give the new unit a try and update review again.

B000FEIOHW-225.review_title: TOO HEAVY for a travel toothbrush
B000FEIOHW-225.review_text: I bought this to use strictly as a travel toothbrush to take to Europe so I wouldn't have to use a plug adapter. It is SO heavy that I returned it...didn't need excess weight in my limited baggage allowance.

B000FEIOHW-297.review_text: Broke so fast. Not even worth sending back. Just annoyed. My daughter said "Can I get the SpongeBob toothbrush I wanted now?"

B000FEIOHW-462.review_text: It stopped working after two months. Tried fresh batteries and new brush head. Safe your self the trouble and get something else.

B000FEIOHW-270.review_text: The price was tempting but after several weeks of use i've detected some serious flaws, for example the bottom cap is not 100% waterproof and the batteries got rusted after few days, same problem with leaks between the replacement head and the rest of the device. It eventually died, this is unusable and unbelieveble how Philips can sell this crap.

B000FEIOHW-473.review_text: Just bought my second unit because the first one did not last and finally died of corrosion. The new unit started acting up after two weeks. The problem is that the brush head and battery compartment do not have a waterproof seal. Water or worse gets in and corrodes and the unit stops working. Leave it for more than a couple of days without cleaning and drying inside and you will have some very slimy growth. Be sure to look at the customer photos supplied for this product ...The leakage and corrosion is exactly what to expect in a very short time. UPDATE 9/8/2013 Despite extreme care to keep unit dry, water gets in and corrodes. Finally contacted Philips after having two fail in less than a year. No problem they said they will send me a replacement. But it is the base and stand of a plug in model they are sending -- THEY NO LONGER OFFER THIS BATTERY MODEL

B000FEIOHW-170.review_text: Bought the battery operated Sonicare in February, 2013. Fourth identical unit I purchased. Used it three times on trips. Changed batteries once. (My job is not very friendly to my nails either!) Tip: putting the Miracle Gel top coat over your cheap $2 polishes will also help you squeeze an extra few days out of those colors. I am very happy with my purchase and would recommend it to a friend.

B01IMEH6GG-137.review_text: Update: I ordered a couple of months ago and love the set of 6 I got. Then I ordered again thinking I'd get at least slightly different ones. Nope! I got the exact same shades again. And I mean EXACTLY the same shades as last time. So no, I wouldn't call it "random" by any stretch of the imagination and no, I'd not order this set of polish again. I like it but not enough to get a third set of the exact same polish again. The set I received had 3 bottles that were various shades of pink (#419, #279,#339), a light green (Prince Char-mint #754), Scarlet red (#429), and Head Bang (#199). Out of the 6, I can honestly say that I love the scarlet red, the light green and the wonderful chocolate color of Head Bang. I didn't get the top coat I requested and was hoping for but I'm okay with that because if I only really liked 2 of the colors I'd have already gotten my moneys worth. When you order this you have to keep in mind, you may not like the colors you get because you are letting someone else pick what you end up with. I am a darker skinned person but I love wearing all colors, no matter the shade, and you kind of have to have that mindset before ordering this. At the same time, keep in mind the cost of one bottle of this polish. It's totally worth it to me if all I have to buy separately is the topcoat. Honestly, if I knew I could get a whole different set of colors, I'd order another random set even if I only get 2 or 3 that I totally love. It's worth it.

These clips are intended for hair-styling purposes more so than using IN a hairstyle if you get what I mean. I probably wouldn't wear one out-and-about but I do use them for sectioning off my hair when I'm blow-drying, curling, or straightening it. Also nice for using to get hair away from face while applying makeup or washing your face. The "grip" power these have on your hair is like nothing I've ever had in a hair clip. The word "clamp" in the product title is accurate. These do not budge or shift, even in straight hair. They really lock your hair in, I think the triangular nature of the teeth on the clips has something to do with that. Very versatile clips that I will most definitely get a lot of use out of, and priced well for the amount you get.
